title: Fisher–Rao Geodesic Attention: Exact Constant-Curvature Kernels for Sequence Models at Near-Matmul Cost
abstract: First public release. Preprint + fully reproducible codebase (CPU, ~2.5h): exact constant-curvature attention kernels derived from the Fisher–Rao metric of distributional token representations. Isotropic-Gaussian hyperbolic kernel at near-matmul cost (2.3x standard attention vs 28x for naive formulations) Headline result: curvature-ordered accuracy on Dyck-2 length extrapolation, +2.10pp over Euclidean across 20 paired seeds (p = 1.9e-10), widening to +4.7pp at 46x model scale Threshold-gated parameter efficiency: equal accuracy at ~3.9x fewer parameters (d_h >= 16) Natural-data transfer: far length-extrapolation on real Python source, pre-registered endpoint met at n=20 seeds (p = 0.0037) with a diagnosis-driven stabilized variant Seven pre-specified negative results reported in full 17 experiment scripts, all raw outputs, interactive 3D geometry visualization

title: Nonlinear pluggable optics: Digital signal processing-free Intensity Modulated Direct Detection links using analog photonic Next Generation Reservoir Computing
abstract: In this work, we propose a Nonlinear Pluggable Optic (NLPO) transceiver that combines the low latency and low power consumption of Linear Pluggable Optics (LPO) with the range and robustness of digital signal processing (DSP)-based transceivers. The proposed NLPO uses an analog photonic Next-Generation Reservoir Computing (NGRC) architecture, constructed on a photonic integrated circuit (PIC), to compensate for electrical-domain distortions as well as optical-channel impairments from chromatic dispersion and Kerr nonlinearity. Focusing on a simulated 50 GBd PAM-4 link, we find that the NGRC-based NLPO not only extends the range of LPO, but actually outperforms DSP-based solutions as well. Our simulations reveal two key advantages compared to DSP-based Intensity Modulation/Direct Detection (IM/DD) links: (1) the NGRC can take advantage of the optical phase information without requiring a local oscillator and (2) the NGRC can optically sample the transmitted data well above the symbol rate without requiring high-bandwidth electronics. This work showcases the potential for photonic NGRCs to outperform state-of-the-art digital solutions in real-world applications and opens a path to low-latency, lower-power IM/DD links at ranges of 10s of km.

title: O'ZBEK TILI PUNKTUATSIYASINING LINGVISTIK ASOSLARI VA UNI AVTOMATIK TIKLASH MODELLARI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu tezisda o‘zbek tilida punktuatsiyani avtomatik tiklash muammosi lingvistik va kompyuter lingvistikasi nuqtayi nazaridan qisqa tahlil qilinadi. Punktuatsion belgilar faqat grafik ajratkich emas, balki sintaktik tuzilish, mazmuniy munosabat va kommunikativ maqsadni ifodalovchi lingvistik vosita sifatida talqin qilinadi. O‘zbek tilining agglutinativ tabiati, grammatik shakllarning axborot yuklamasi va gap qurilishining xususiyatlari punktuatsion qarorlarning kontekstga bog‘liqligini kuchaytiradi. Shu asosda punktuatsiyani tiklash tokenlar orasidagi chegaralarda tegishli punktuatsion sinfni aniqlash vazifasi sifatida modellashtiriladi. Transformer va CRF modellarining uyg‘unligi kontekstual hamda ketma-ketlik xususiyatlarini hisobga olish imkonini beradi, yakuniy qaror Viterbi algoritmi orqali olinadi. Manbadagi tajriba ma’lumotlariga ko‘ra, o‘quv to‘plami 1 379 986 token, validatsiya to‘plami 179 371 token, news-test 87 721 token, reference-test 6 821 so‘z va ASR-test 6 417 so‘zni qamrab oladi. ASR sharoitida WER 14,8 foizni tashkil etadi. Tezisda manbada berilmagan model natijalari sun’iy ravishda kiritilmaydi. Kalit so‘zlar: o‘zbek tili, punktuatsiya, punktuatsion birlik, kompyuter lingvistikasi, korpus lingvistikasi, Transformer, CRF, Viterbi, ASR, sintaksis, semantika, pragmatika. Аннотация. В настоящих тезисах кратко анализируется проблема автоматического восстановления пунктуации в узбекском языке с позиций лингвистики и компьютерной лингвистики. Пунктуационные знаки рассматриваются не только как графические разделители, но и как лингвистические средства, выражающие синтаксическую структуру, смысловые отношения и коммуникативную цель высказывания. Агглютинативная природа узбекского языка, информационная нагрузка грамматических форм и особенности структуры предложения усиливают контекстуальную зависимость пунктуационных решений. На этой основе восстановление пунктуации моделируется как задача определения соответствующего пунктуационного класса на границах между токенами. Сочетание моделей Transformer и CRF позволяет учитывать как контекстуальные, так и последовательностные характеристики, а окончательное решение определяется с помощью алгоритма Витерби. Согласно экспериментальным данным источника, обучающая выборка включает 1 379 986 токенов, валидационная выборка — 179 371 токен, news-test — 87 721 токен, reference-test — 6 821 слово, а ASR-test — 6 417 слов. В условиях ASR показатель WER составляет 14,8 %. В тезисах не приводятся искусственно сформированные результаты модели, отсутствующие в исходном источнике. Ключевые слова: узбекский язык, пунктуация, пунктуационная единица, компьютерная лингвистика, корпусная лингвистика, Transformer, CRF, Витерби, ASR, синтаксис, семантика, прагматика. Abstract. This thesis provides a brief analysis of the problem of automatic punctuation restoration in the Uzbek language from the perspectives of linguistics and computational linguistics. Punctuation marks are interpreted not merely as graphic separators, but also as linguistic means that express syntactic structure, semantic relations, and the communicative purpose of an utterance. The agglutinative nature of Uzbek, the information load of grammatical forms, and the structural characteristics of sentences increase the contextual dependence of punctuation decisions. On this basis, punctuation restoration is modeled as the task of determining an appropriate punctuation class at token boundaries. The combination of Transformer and CRF models makes it possible to account for both contextual and sequential characteristics, while the final decision is determined using the Viterbi algorithm. According to the experimental data provided in the source, the training set contains 1,379,986 tokens, the validation set contains 179,371 tokens, the news-test set contains 87,721 tokens, the reference-test set contains 6,821 words, and the ASR-test set contains 6,417 words. Under ASR conditions, the WER is 14.8%. The thesis does not introduce artificially generated model results that are not reported in the original source. Keywords: Uzbek language, punctuation, punctuation unit, computational linguistics, corpus linguistics, Transformer, CRF, Viterbi algorithm, ASR, syntax, semantics, pragmatics

Transformer va CRF modellarining uyg‘unligi kontekstual hamda ketma-ketlik xususiyatlarini hisobga olish imkonini beradi, yakuniy qaror Viterbi algoritmi orqali olinadi. Manbadagi tajriba ma’lumotlariga ko‘ra, o‘quv to‘plami 1 379 986 token, validatsiya to‘plami 179 371 token, news-test 87 721 token, reference-test 6 821 so‘z va ASR-test 6 417 so‘zni qamrab oladi. ASR sharoitida WER 14,8 foizni tashkil etadi. Tezisda manbada berilmagan model natijalari sun’iy ravishda kiritilmaydi. Kalit so‘zlar: o‘zbek tili, punktuatsiya, punktuatsion birlik, kompyuter lingvistikasi, korpus lingvistikasi, Transformer, CRF, Viterbi, ASR, sintaksis, semantika, pragmatika. Аннотация. В настоящих тезисах кратко анализируется проблема автоматического восстановления пунктуации в узбекском языке с позиций лингвистики и компьютерной лингвистики. Пунктуационные знаки рассматриваются не только как графические разделители, но и как лингвистические средства, выражающие синтаксическую структуру, смысловые отношения и коммуникативную цель высказывания. Агглютинативная природа узбекского языка, информационная нагрузка грамматических форм и особенности структуры предложения усиливают контекстуальную зависимость пунктуационных решений. На этой основе восстановление пунктуации моделируется как задача определения соответствующего пунктуационного класса на границах между токенами. Сочетание моделей Transformer и CRF позволяет учитывать как контекстуальные, так и последовательностные характеристики, а окончательное решение определяется с помощью алгоритма Витерби. Согласно экспериментальным данным источника, обучающая выборка включает 1 379 986 токенов, валидационная выборка — 179 371 токен, news-test — 87 721 токен, reference-test — 6 821 слово, а ASR-test — 6 417 слов. В условиях ASR показатель WER составляет 14,8 %. В тезисах не приводятся искусственно сформированные результаты модели, отсутствующие в исходном источнике. Ключевые слова: узбекский язык, пунктуация, пунктуационная единица, компьютерная лингвистика, корпусная лингвистика, Transformer, CRF, Витерби, ASR, синтаксис, семантика, прагматика. Abstract. This thesis provides a brief analysis of the problem of automatic punctuation restoration in the Uzbek language from the perspectives of linguistics and computational linguistics. Punctuation marks are interpreted not merely as graphic separators, but also as linguistic means that express syntactic structure, semantic relations, and the communicative purpose of an utterance. The agglutinative nature of Uzbek, the information load of grammatical forms, and the structural characteristics of sentences increase the contextual dependence of punctuation decisions. On this basis, punctuation restoration is modeled as the task of determining an appropriate punctuation class at token boundaries. The combination of Transformer and CRF models makes it possible to account for both contextual and sequential characteristics, while the final decision is determined using the Viterbi algorithm. According to the experimental data provided in the source, the training set contains 1,379,986 tokens, the validation set contains 179,371 tokens, the news-test set contains 87,721 tokens, the reference-test set contains 6,821 words, and the ASR-test set contains 6,417 words. Under ASR conditions, the WER is 14.8%. The thesis does not introduce artificially generated model results that are not reported in the original source. title: From knowledge retrieval to generation: a comprehensive study of RAG's architectures, evolution, and applications
abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning, but their reliance on static parametric knowledge still leads to knowledge staleness, hallucinations, limited domain adaptability, weak traceability, and high updating costs in knowledge-intensive scenarios. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps address these limitations by incorporating external knowledge sources into the generation process, making it an important approach for improving factual grounding, knowledge timeliness, and evidence traceability. However, existing RAG research is increasingly fragmented across architectures, retrieval and generation strategies, evaluation methods, application scenarios, deployment constraints, and security risks. To provide a systematic understanding of this field, this survey reviews RAG research through a structured and transparent review protocol. We organize the review around three major dimensions: the system stack and paradigm evolution of RAG, evaluation methods and application evidence, and practical deployment and security challenges. Specifically, we analyze the core components of RAG systems, synthesize their evolution from Naive RAG to Agentic RAG, examine evaluation metrics and stress-testing protocols, summarize benchmark datasets and domain applications, and discuss deployment constraints and emerging risks such as prompt injection, data poisoning, retrieval hijacking, privacy leakage, and citation laundering. This survey provides a taxonomy-oriented, evaluation-aware, and deployment-conscious reference for understanding the development, limitations, and future directions of RAG systems.

abstract: The El-Rakhawi Holographic Causal Memory Architecture (HCMA) revolutionizes AI memory by shifting from spatial storage to holographic boundary encoding. Addressing the curse of dimensionality and sequential retrieval bottlenecks, HCMA maps high-dimensional causal Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) onto a lower-dimensional manifold using Holographic Reduced Representations and Tree Tensor Networks. It establishes the Holographic Memory Capacity Bound, proving memory scales with physical boundary surface area rather than volume, enabling exponential compression. Retrieval leverages physical wave-interference, reducing time complexity from sequential O(N) to parallel optical propagation time, effectively achieving O(1) logical retrieval. Crucially, HCMA introduces the Thermodynamics of Reversible Memory Reconfiguration, utilizing unitary transformations to uncompute and reallocate memory states. This defers the Landauer limit penalty, minimizing heat dissipation during continuous learning. HCMA provides the ultimate framework for storing planet-scale causal world models on a single chip, enabling energy-efficient Artificial General Intelligence.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI FLUIDIC CAUSAL INTELLIGENCE ARCHITECTURE (FCIA): IN-VIVO MICROFLUIDIC RESERVOIR COMPUTING VIA CHAOTIC ADVECTION AND REACTION-DIFFUSION DYNAMICS
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Fluidic Causal Intelligence Architecture (FCIA) shifts computing from solid-state electronics to liquid-state computing in biological environments. It utilizes microfluidic networks for continuous-time causal inference with zero external electrical power. Harnessing Lagrangian chaotic advection via 3D spatial modulation and biocompatible reaction-diffusion dynamics using enzymatic cascades or DNA strand displacement, the system acts as a physical reservoir computer. It processes temporal biological signals to autonomously actuate therapeutic responses. Engineered with ultra-low hydraulic resistance to prevent hemolysis, it operates on ambient biological energy. The algorithm minimizes the El-Rakhawi Fluidic Causal Loss, enforcing Advection-Diffusion-Reaction dynamics. Performance is quantified by the El-Rakhawi Fluidic Computational Efficiency Metric in bits per Joule. This enables biocompatible, battery-less smart implants and environmental nodes, bridging AI, fluid physics, chemistry, and neuroscience.

title: Trustworthy Federated Learning for Cybersecurity: A Three-Level Assurance Taxonomy, Design-Space Audit, and Source-Linked Critical Review.
abstract: This repository contains the supporting evidence and reproducibility materials for the manuscript “Trustworthy Federated Learning for Cybersecurity: A Three-Level Assurance Taxonomy, Design-Space Audit, and Source-Linked Critical Review.” The package includes: A study-feature matrix covering 20 studies and 18 features. A source-linked audit ledger containing 360 study-feature judgments, with source references, evidence locators, and coding notes. Feature definitions, coding guidance, and mappings between the original and current study identifiers. Supporting Information in PDF and LaTeX formats. Python scripts for generating figures, preparing data partitions, and checking the experimental implementation. Documentation, validation results, and file checksums. These materials allow reviewers and researchers to inspect the recorded evidence, understand the coding decisions, and reproduce the documented data-derived outputs. The package contains literature-review data and supporting code; it does not include third-party raw cybersecurity datasets. Synthetic examples are provided for software checks and do not represent real-data experimental findings. Internal consistency checks do not constitute independent re-coding or fresh verification of every cited source. The README explains the package’s provenance, usage, scope, and remaining limitations.

title: Conceptual Blueprint: A 3-Part Triad for Behavioral Resilience in Hectic Environments
abstract: This technical specification outlines a novel, non-linear multi-agent model orchestration system (Architecture Reference Code: BEHAVIORAL-TRIAD-ARCH-2026) designed to maintain conversational flow and deep contextual tracking during abrupt human behavioral, psychological, or situational shifts. Traditional Large Language Models (LLMs) are structurally biased toward linear, predictable, and sanitized inputs; they break down or experience latency spikes when a user transitions from standard communicative baselines to frantic, compressed, or high-panic communication styles under immense stress. To overcome these rigid constraints, the architecture deploys an interwoven, three-part runtime engine that handles information routing based on real-time human behavior metrics: the Altered Adaptive Relative Model (AARM), the Young Openly Evolving Unit (YOEU), and the Unfiltered Odd-Minded Brother Model (UMB). By mapping human evolutionary sensory-gating and biological data compression mechanisms into an engineering specification, this framework enables AI to adapt dynamically to the human condition, emotional nuance, and crisis states without forcing unhelpful clarification cycles.

title: Volume IV: Modular Cryogenics, Cryo-CMOS Control and Molecular Entanglement: Hardware Pathways for Quantum Molecular Simulation
abstract: This fourth volume synthesises the hardware and information-theoretic threads that followed Volume III. It examines modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control electronics as complementary solutions to the scaling bottlenecks that limit quantum processors, then maps those capabilities onto the concrete requirements of quantum molecular simulation. Memory specifications (coherence time, fidelity, efficiency, multimode capacity and latency) are related to the circuit depths and intermediate-state storage needed for electronic-structure and dynamics algorithms. Molecular entanglement entropy is analysed as both a diagnostic of multi-reference character and a quantitative driver of those hardware demands. The 2025 Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion experiment that reconstructed orbital von Neumann entropies for the vinylene-carbonate + singlet-oxygen reaction path is reviewed, together with the purifying and resource-reducing effects of fermionic superselection rules. The volume concludes that the modular cryogenic and cryo-CMOS stack, when combined with the memory and entanglement metrics already established, supplies a practical pathway toward chemically relevant quantum simulations without requiring a single definitive quantum-advantage date.

title: Autonomous agents and multi-agent systems: a comprehensive review
abstract: Autonomous agents and multi-agent systems have rapidly advanced with the integration of large language models (LLMs), enabling increasingly capable reasoning, planning, tool use, and collaboration. However, the field remains fragmented by inconsistent architectural terminology, limited cross-domain comparison, and heterogeneous evaluation practices. This review addresses these gaps through a two-stage PRISMA-informed search combining Scopus with structured manual screening, covering 107 peer-reviewed original studies published between 2018 and 2026. We propose a unified five-module architecture comprising profile, memory, planning, action, and security; systematically compare agent capabilities across ten application domains; and organize evaluation practices into six dimensions: task performance, efficiency, quality, robustness, safety, and interpretability. The review identifies two recurring patterns across domains: explicit integration of domain knowledge consistently improves performance, while planner–executor–reflector role specialization appears across diverse applications. However, technical performance often exceeds validated real-world utility, with robustness, safety, and interpretability remaining particularly under-evaluated. These findings provide a common basis for understanding, comparing, and developing autonomous agents and highlight priorities for more reliable and practically deployable systems.

title: O'ZBEK TILI MORFOANALIZATORIDA FE'L BO'LMAGAN SO'ZLAR+FE'L TARKIBLI QO'SHMA FE'LLAR VA SO'Z BIRIKMALARINI FARQLASH MODELI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Mazkur maqolada o‘zbek tili morfoanalizatorida fe’l bo‘lmagan so‘z + fe’l tarkibli qo‘shma fe’llar hamda erkin so‘z birikmalarini avtomatik farqlash masalasi tadqiq etilgan. Ushbu birliklarning shaklan o‘xshashligi morfologik tahlil va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash jarayonida muayyan qiyinchiliklarni yuzaga keltirishi asoslangan. Qo‘shma fe’l va so‘z birikmalarini farqlash uchun leksik, morfologik, sintaktik va semantik mezonlarga asoslangan lingvistik-kompyuter modeli taklif etilgan. Model leksik tekshiruv, qoidaviy filtrlar hamda statistik/mashinali o‘qitish modulini o‘z ichiga oladi. Tadqiqotda COMPOUND_VERB, NOUN+VERB_PHRASE va UNSURE teglari asosida annotatsiya va avtomatik tasniflash mexanizmi ishlab chiqilgan. Mazkur modelni o‘zbek tili morfoanalizatoriga integratsiya qilish orqali qo‘shma fe’llar va erkin so‘z birikmalarini aniqroq ajratish hamda morfologik tahlil sifatini oshirish imkoniyati ko‘rsatilgan. Kalit so‘zlar: o‘zbek tili, morfoanalizator, qo‘shma fe’l, so‘z birikmasi, fe’l, morfologik tahlil, tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash, mashinali o‘qitish, lingvistik model, avtomatik tasniflash, teg, COMPOUND_VERB. Аннотация. В статье исследуется проблема автоматического различения сложных глаголов, образованных по модели «не-глагольное слово + глагол», и свободных словосочетаний в морфологическом анализаторе узбекского языка. Обосновывается, что формальное сходство данных конструкций создает определенные трудности при морфологическом анализе и обработке естественного языка. Для их дифференциации предлагается лингвистико-компьютерная модель, основанная на лексических, морфологических, синтаксических и семантических признаках. Модель включает лексическую проверку, систему правил и статистический/машинно-обучаемый модуль. Разработан механизм аннотирования и автоматической классификации на основе тегов COMPOUND_VERB, NOUN+VERB_PHRASE и UNSURE. Показана возможность интеграции предложенной модели в морфологический анализатор узбекского языка для более точного различения сложных глаголов и свободных словосочетаний, а также повышения качества морфологического анализа. Ключевые слова: узбекский язык, морфологический анализатор, сложный глагол, словосочетание, глагол, морфологический анализ, обработка естественного языка, машинное обучение, лингвистическая модель, автоматическая классификация, тегирование, COMPOUND_VERB. Abstract. This article examines the problem of automatically distinguishing compound verbs formed according to the “non-verb word + verb” pattern from free word combinations in an Uzbek morphological analyzer. It is shown that the formal similarity of these constructions creates difficulties in morphological analysis and natural language processing. A linguistic-computational model based on lexical, morphological, syntactic, and semantic features is proposed to differentiate the two types of constructions. The model incorporates lexical verification, rule-based filters, and a statistical/machine-learning module. An annotation and automatic classification mechanism based on the tags COMPOUND_VERB, NOUN+VERB_PHRASE, and UNSURE is developed. The study demonstrates that integrating the proposed model into an Uzbek morphological analyzer can improve the automatic distinction between compound verbs and free word combinations and enhance the accuracy of morphological analysis. В статье исследуется проблема автоматического различения сложных глаголов, образованных по модели «не-глагольное слово + глагол», и свободных словосочетаний в морфологическом анализаторе узбекского языка. Abstract. This article examines the problem of automatically distinguishing compound verbs formed according to the “non-verb word + verb” pattern from free word combinations in an Uzbek morphological analyzer. It is shown that the formal similarity of these constructions creates difficulties in morphological analysis and natural language processing. A linguistic-computational model based on lexical, morphological, syntactic, and semantic features is proposed to differentiate the two types of constructions. The model incorporates lexical verification, rule-based filters, and a statistical/machine-learning module. An annotation and automatic classification mechanism based on the tags COMPOUND_VERB, NOUN+VERB_PHRASE, and UNSURE is developed. The study demonstrates that integrating the proposed model into an Uzbek morphological analyzer can improve the automatic distinction between compound verbs and free word combinations and enhance the accuracy of morphological analysis. title: Protocol-granularity classification of Linux kernel network-stack CVEs, with retrieval and classification scripts (Netshim)
abstract: Classification of 637 Linux kernel network-stack CVEs by the protocol subsystem containing the defect, used to quantify attack-surface reduction at protocol granularity. Records were retrieved from the NVD REST API 2.0 on 2026-10-16 using two queries - the Linux kernel CPE match and the Linux kernel CNA source identifier - yielding 25,612 unique kernel CVE records. 24,975 were excluded as not belonging to an in-kernel IP-family protocol implementation, leaving 637. Of these, 541 fall in subsystems a TCP-only stack does not implement, 187 of them reachable by a remote packet-sending adversary. v2 adds the performance re-run underlying Section 6: 10 trials across 6 concurrency levels, 2 payload sizes and both stacks, measured on the paper's host with DPDK 21.11.9 against the hardened build. One case (trial 1, netshim, 1kb, c=1) returned NA because DPDK initialisation raced the first request and is excluded from the analysis. The CVE corpus is unchanged from v1

title: Quantized Mereology
abstract: This paper investigates quantized mereology, which merges quantum information theory with classical mereology, the formal analysis of the part-whole relationship. It emphasizes that information about crisp mereological relations is captured by classical bits, whereas mereological vagueness involves the use of quantum bits, or qubits, to capture mereological information. Transitioning from classical bits to qubits offers a new understanding of part-whole relations among entities that are subject to mereological vagueness. This paper methodically studies the quantized mereology that arises from the classical RCC5 formalism, one of the most widely studied formalisms in Qualitative Reasoning (QR), a subfield of Artificial Intelligence. The argument is made that this method can be extended to quantize more sophisticated QR formalisms, mirroring how strategies are used in physics to transition from classical to quantum systems. The study explores: (i) the conversion of bits to qubits while understanding that these (qu)bits convey mereological information; (ii) the representation of qubit states via set partitions, acknowledging that set theory aligns more closely with classical logic than with the complex vector spaces employed in quantum physics; (iii) demonstrating that classical QR formalisms can be seen as special cases within quantized formalisms; and (iv) showing that qubits more effectively encapsulate information about vague phenomena.

title: Cognitive Surrender and Epistemic Agency in AI-Mediated Education: Code, Results, and Reproducibility Materials
abstract: This repository accompanies “Cognitive Surrender and Epistemic Agency in AI-Mediated Education.” The study combines a conceptual account of cognitive surrender with an exploratory analysis of 16,851 student–LLM interactions from 203 StudyChat users. It examines reliance-oriented interaction patterns, their relationship with visible struggle, contextual variation, and prediction from early interactions. It also proposes a delegation boundary to help educational AI preserve learner judgment and meaningful participation. The package contains analysis code, aggregate results, reproducibility instructions, and sensitivity analyses, including checks that exclude low-context prompting from the Reliance Index. The findings characterize observable behavior without establishing cognitive surrender, diminished learning, or loss of agency. The original StudyChat dataset is not redistributed and must be obtained separately from its source.

title: Volume V: Anatomical Dissection of Quantum Ecosystems: Hardware, Control, Memory and Molecular Pathways against Ecosystem Claims
abstract: This fifth volume performs an anatomical dissection of the claim that quantum leadership will be determined by the construction of a complete ecosystem (hardware, software, networking, sensing, talent and industrialization) rather than by qubit count alone. Each element of the claim is examined against the concrete technical stack developed in the preceding volumes of the series and against established protocols in cryogenic engineering, control electronics, quantum memory and molecular simulation. Modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control are shown to be necessary but not sufficient conditions for the hardware layer; quantum memory specifications and molecular entanglement entropy supply the quantitative criteria that convert raw processor capacity into usable molecular applications; and the dual-clock framing established earlier demonstrates that ecosystem construction is already constrained by migration and architectural lead times that are running independently of any single advantage date. The analysis concludes that ecosystem rhetoric is operationally meaningful only when it is reduced to the measurable interfaces among modular cryogenics, cryogenic control, memory metrics and chemically relevant entanglement.

title: E=mc²=i, the entangled pair: dated predictions for the mass of one ebit and for the moment the teleportation heat appears
abstract: Dated predictions, registered before any experiment designed to test them. This is the author's hypothesis. It is not proven, it is not established physics, and it is not a theory of everything. Every prediction lies below the sensitivity of current experiments, so a null result at today's sensitivity neither supports nor refutes it. Building on E=mc²=i (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23415364), where one bit carries the mass of its Landauer energy, kT ln 2 / c², this record applies that formula to an entangled pair. By the author's choice, one maximally entangled pair (one ebit) carries n = 1 bit, held by the relation between the halves, not by either half: 3.2 × 10⁻³⁸ kg at 300 K. Six pair predictions follow (EP1 to EP6: weigh the pair, drop the pair, heat at the detectors, the pair as fuel, locked bits in silicon against the entangled pair, and superdense coding), each set against what standard physics predicts. It also registers P12: the 2 kT ln 2 of heat per teleportation (E=mc²=i P7, cited unchanged) appears at the moment of the Bell-state measurement, even while the outcome record is kept and never erased. A delayed-erasure test is proposed that separates the measurement moment from the record erasure. Open questions are stated as open. Foundation: this record builds on the author's earlier record E=mc²=i (all versions: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23414461), which is itself untested. Its predictions hold only if E=mc²=i holds; a confirmation of E=mc²=i would not by itself confirm the choice n = 1. Falsifier, stated plainly: no excess mass (n = 0) is the result that proves the entangled-pair claim wrong. Prior work: Melvin M. Vopson's mass-energy-information equivalence principle, a stored bit with mass kT ln 2 / c² (Vopson 2019, AIP Advances 9, 095206; test protocol Vopson 2022, AIP Advances 12, 035311), proposed and not yet confirmed. This record shares that vision from another perspective: the bit held by the relation in an entangled pair, one shared bit, rather than by a memory. Bits = quanta is an author's postulate used within the E=mc²=i framework and should not be interpreted as a statement of established quantum information theory.

title: Exact minimum distances of 27 quantum LDPC codes from recent papers and the qLDPC challenge board (d = 14 to 24)
abstract: This deposit gives exact minimum distances for 27 quantum CSS codes. For each one, the published value was only an upper bound, an interval or an estimate, and as far as we can find the exact value had not been posted. The codes: weight-5 bivariate bicycle codes from J. Cruz-Benito, arXiv:2610.06623: [[432,4]] d = 23, both [[420,4]] classes d = 22, [[420,6]] d = 16, [[432,8]] d = 15, [[420,8]] d = 14; twisted-torus codes from Liang, Liu, Song and Chen, arXiv:2503.03827: d = 22 for [[234,4]], [[246,4]], [[258,4]], [[264,4]], [[280,6]], [[306,8]], [[310,10]], [[312,8]], [[324,8]], [[336,10]], [[342,8]]; covering-graph BB codes from Symons, Rajput and Browne, arXiv:2511.13560: [[140,8]] d = 14, [[192,14]] d = 16, [[192,20]] d = 16, [[224,26]] d = 14; qLDPC challenge board entries: [[454,8]] d = 17, [[316,8]] d = 16, [[280,8]] d = 15, [[210,26]] d = 14, [[510,16]] (board 510-16-24) d = 24; the [[510,16]] generalized bicycle code of Webster, Smith and Cohen (arXiv:2511.15989) and Iceberg Quantum's Pinnacle architecture (arXiv:2602.11457): d = 24. The value 24 is printed there as a conjectured family value; this deposit adds a verification. Method: two separately written exhaustive searches (Python/numba and C), anchored connected-cluster enumeration after Dumer, Kovalev and Pryadko, with symmetry anchoring after Rowshan and Devitt. For 25 codes, each search finds no logical of weight d-1 or less on either side. For the two [[510,16]] codes, both searches exclude weight 22 or less, and since every column has weight 3, every logical has even weight, which rules out 23. Explicit weight-d logicals give the matching upper bound. No machine-checkable certificate is included, so this is a search-based result. The two programs share one method, and LIMITATIONS.md says so. A bug in the second program's quick bound was found during review; it affected codes with column degree above 3. It was fixed, and those codes were rerun. Already-known values are credited, not claimed. G. Lee's bicycle-race database has exact values for codes equivalent to 288-8-20, 266-6-22, 300-8-22 and 210-10-16. Liang et al. give exact values for 248-10-18 and 180-8-16. Our runs agree with these. Contents: code files with check matrices, witnesses, orbits and automorphism generators; both programs; all run logs; one-command quick check (quick_check.sh); hostile review; LIMITATIONS.md. Work done with AI assistants (Claude and ChatGPT) on a home PC.

title: Emergent Behaviour in Financial Markets
abstract: Abstract Some properties of so-called complex or collective systems can be observed to emerge from the interactions of elementary agents. This phenomenon, known as emergent behaviour, has long since been studied in the most diverse disciplines, with recent growing awareness from the formal methods community about the opportunity of opening up to seemingly distant disciplines with appropriate technology for computer-aided reasoning. Different peculiar elements of complexity make automated reasoning on these systems particularly challenging. We consider electronic financial markets to drive our discussion. We identify and structure the sources of complexity to tackle in order to provide computational support for the analysis of emergent phenomena. We refrain from evaluating the suitability of specific technical solutions or frameworks of preference, which would as usual require simplifying assumptions and divert from the actual phenomenon of interest. Rather, we elaborate on possible alternatives to handle some of the main technical aspects involved in automated analysis, while retaining a solid and concrete interpretation of the domain, and in doing so outline a more systematic research program for the formal specification and analysis of market mechanisms.

title: REIMAGINING MARKETING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CASE STUDIES AND MANAGERIAL INSIGHTS
abstract: This document explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in marketing, emphasizing its widespread adoption across businesses of all sizes and the complexities involved in its implementation, such as data privacy concerns and algorithmic bias. The research methodology involves a detailed analysis of real-world case studies from diverse industries, examining how organizations utilize AI-powered tools like machine learning and predictive analytics to enhance customer engagement and optimize marketing strategies. The conclusion highlights AI's potential to create personalized experiences and automate processes, while also stressing the importance of addressing ethical challenges and maintaining consumer trust. It calls for the development of strategies that effectively leverage AI capabilities while prioritizing ethical considerations, and suggests future research directions focused on the long-term impacts of AI on customer loyalty and best practices for integrating AI technologies into existing marketing frameworks.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Technical Project Management: A Critical Incident Study
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports project management tasks in technical, technological and innovation-oriented environments. This paper examines how AI is used in technical project management through a qualitative critical incident technique study. The analysis focuses on a technical subsample of five project managers and 26 selected incidents from information technology, vehicle-related technical projects, technology transfer, innovation management and cybersecurity. The findings show that AI mainly functions as a supportive tool in documentation, information processing, data analysis, idea generation and decision preparation. Its strongest value appears in the planning and execution phases, where it improves efficiency, structure and communication. However, the incidents also reveal risks related to data quality, inaccurate outputs, legal constraints, trust and user acceptance. This study concludes that AI can create value in technical projects only when its use remains combined with human validation, professional judgement and clear responsibility.

title: Adaptive Reinforced Elite Gray Wolf Optimization for Robotic Path Planning and Football Pass-Quality Prediction
abstract: Complex optimization problems in engineering and data-driven modeling require effective exploration, stable convergence, and adaptability across different decision representations. This study proposes an Adaptive Reinforced Elite Gray Wolf Optimizer (AREGWO) that combines opposition-based initialization, nonlinear convergence control, reinforced elite guidance, adaptive weak perturbation, stagnation-aware partial restart, and greedy elite inheritance. AREGWO is evaluated through CEC2022 benchmark optimization, synthetic 2D constrained robotic path planning, and football pass-quality prediction. On CEC2022, AREGWO ranks second among nine algorithms in the Friedman test and significantly outperforms seven of eight competitors in the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, while L-SHADE remains the strongest baseline. Component-wise ablation shows that the six mechanisms provide complementary and problem-dependent contributions. In robotic path planning, 30 independent runs on six random maps yield a six-map average path length of 134.38 m, which is 3.61–5.12% shorter than those obtained by the four population-based baselines and 1.08% shorter than A*, with a 100% success rate in all tested environments. For football pass-quality prediction, AREGWO is coupled with TabM for outer-level hyperparameter optimization of a predefined pass-quality reference score. AREGWO-TabM achieves an RMSE of 0.445, an MSE of 0.198, and an R2 of 0.920, providing the best RMSE, MSE, and R2 among the evaluated neural models, although ResNet attains a lower MAE. These results demonstrate the competitive search capability of AREGWO across the numerical, synthetic spatial, and model-level optimization settings evaluated in this study.

title: Computational Intelligence and Python Programming
abstract: This book on computational intelligence and Python programming serve as comprehensive guides to nature-inspired computing, machine learning, and advancedproblem-solving techniques. The first core focus of such a text establishes the theoretical foundation of computational intelligence (CI), covering key paradigms likeartificial neural networks, fuzzy logic systems, evolutionary algorithms (such asgenetic algorithms), and swarm intelligence. Rather than relying on rigid algorithmic rules, these books explain how computers mimic biological processes to adapt,learn, and make decisions under uncertain or incomplete data conditions.The second core focus bridges these theoretical concepts directly into practicethrough hands-on Python programming. Utilizing ecosystem libraries like NumPy,SciPy, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and specialized CI packages, the text guides readersthrough building, training, and optimizing intelligent models from scratch. Bycombining mathematical rigor with clear code examples, it enables developers, datascientists, and researchers to design scalable applications across predictive analytics,robotics, natural language processing, and automated decision-making systems.

title: INTERACT streaming speech-to-sign benchmark (s2sbench)
abstract: Open benchmark that measures how streaming speech recognition affects a real-time International Sign avatar that plays one dictionary sign at a time and fingerspells the other words, as in the INTERACT meeting platform developed under the CORTEX2 Horizon Europe programme. It replays meeting audio of the AMI Meeting Corpus in real time through four streaming methods with Whisper (fixed chunks, pause-based utterances, LocalAgreement-2 and AlignAtt), maps the released words to International Sign with three text-to-sign rules, simulates the avatar's playback and scores the transcript, the signs and their timing, with a perfect-transcript analysis of the 16 evaluation meetings. The release contains the code, the configurations, the unit tests, the run files of every streaming run, all results, the figures and the build script of the accompanying article, 'How live transcription shapes a signing avatar: an open benchmark of streaming speech recognition for real-time International Sign translation in meetings' (submitted to Open Research Europe), whose shorter preprint is https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202610.0572.v1. The code is under the MIT licence and the run files, results, dictionary metadata and figures are under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.md).

title: AI for Public Benefit: Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Using Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning for Crisis Management and Public Policy in India
abstract: Social media has transformed public disclosure in India by providing real-time perceptions of public opinion, which are valuable for crisis management and public policy formation. Using the Farmers Protest Tweets Dataset, this research examines the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) sentiment analysis. A comparative study found that fine-tuned IndicBERT outperformed LSTM and Logistic Regression in sentiment classification. Sentiment distribution showed 48.5% positive, 29.5% neutral, and 22.0% negative tweets. Analysis revealed positive sentiment toward the protest movement and negative sentiment toward the government and media. The findings support real-time public opinion monitoring, crisis detection, and policy decision-making.

title: Synthesizing event semantics for temporal knowledge graph reasoning
abstract: Most existing temporal knowledge graph reasoning (TKGR) methods primarily model structural dependencies and temporal dynamics from historical facts, while fact-aligned event semantics, such as hierarchical event types and background contexts, are often underexploited. This may result in incomplete semantic characterization of relations and entities, making it difficult to distinguish semantically similar event relations and contextually plausible entity candidates. To investigate this issue, this paper proposes ES-TKGR, an event-semantics-enhanced model for TKGR, which constructs and integrates event semantics aligned with TKG facts to model implicit dependencies among facts. Specifically, ES-TKGR consists of three key components. First, the E vent T ype H ierarchical C onstraint E ncoding (ETHCE) module incorporates hierarchical event type semantics to strengthen relation modeling by introducing a hierarchical distance-aware prototype contrastive objective over relation representations, while promoting semantic interaction among facts through explicit type-aware connections. Second, the S tatic K nowledge G raph E ncoding (SKGE) module incorporates event background semantics by constructing a global static graph from historical facts and aligning it with background knowledge, thereby capturing time-independent global interaction patterns. Third, an adaptive fusion module integrates dynamic features from ETHCE and static features from SKGE to obtain unified representations. To evaluate future entity and relation prediction under fact-aligned event semantics, we construct four ICEWS-based TKG datasets aligned with event semantic information. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that ES-TKGR outperforms or remains competitive with recent baselines, underscoring the effectiveness of fact-aligned event semantics for enriching entity and relation representations and modeling implicit fact dependencies in TKGR.

title: Badpatches: routing-aware backdoor attacks on vision mixture-of-experts
abstract: Abstract Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have gained significant traction for reducing computational costs in deep neural networks by activating only a sparse subset of parameters during inference. While this efficiency makes MoE highly attractive for scaling vision tasks, its patch-based processing mechanism inherently disrupts traditional, routing-agnostic backdoor attacks by fragmenting or discarding adversarial triggers. To expose the vulnerabilities of this architecture, we introduce BadPatches, a novel routing-aware trigger application strategy specifically designed for patch-based MoE (pMoE) models and MoE-based vision transformers. Rather than applying a global pattern across the entire image, BadPatches encapsulates triggers within targeted image patches, ensuring they are consistently routed to and processed by the active experts. Our evaluations demonstrate that BadPatches achieves a high Attack Success Rate (ASR) at lower poisoning rates than routing-agnostic triggers, reaching over 83.2% ASR with a poisoning rate of only 0.01%, and scaling to a 96.8% ASR at 0.05%, while preserving the model’s clean accuracy. Furthermore, the attack remains effective in gray-box scenarios where the adversary lacks complete knowledge of the model’s patch routing configuration. Finally, we evaluate fine-pruning as a potential defense mechanism, revealing that pruning alone is insufficient to mitigate the attack; successful backdoor removal strictly requires the fine-tuning stage. These findings highlight the fragility of sparse vision architectures and underscore the need for routing-aware defenses.

title: Noise-robust discrimination of incoherent point sources with spatial-mode demultiplexing
abstract: We theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate that a reduced spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) measurement using only the two lowest-order Hermite-Gaussian modes exhibits remarkable robustness against background noise in discriminating between a single source and two incoherent point sources. We establish a theoretical framework incorporating uniform background noise and derive an analytical Chernoff exponent expression, showing that SPADE consistently outperforms direct imaging (DI) across all source separations. Experimental results confirm that SPADE-based hypothesis testing approaches the quantum limit even when the background-to-signal photon ratio per pixel is 0.11. This advantage stems from SPADE's ability to concentrate source information into minimal detection modes, reducing the cumulative background noise impact. Our findings provide a practical detection scheme for applications where background noise is inevitable, such as astronomical observations and quantum sensing.

title: Role of Automated Machine Learning approach for lung cancer data classification using modern techniques
abstract: Medical data classification is the process for categorizing healthcare-related information, such as patient records, medical images, and diagnostic results, into distinct groups based on predefined criteria.Machine learning plays a pivotal role by classifying the medical data.Machine learning and deep learning techniques have become indispensable tools in precision healthcare and automated disease diagnosis, enabling accurate clinical decision-making and predictive analytics [22,23,27].leveraging algorithms that can detect pattern automatically from the data and can make predictions with less human interference.ML models unlike traditional method analyze vast amount of medical data, recognize complex patterns , and generalize new cases according to learning.,This paper therefore seeks to produce informed and precise medical data classification strategy for Lung cancer datasets.For lung cancer data classification Machine learning algorithms like Support vector machine(SVM), Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN), Residual Neural Network(ResNet), and Random Forest(RF) are used in this research paper due to their ability to extract meaningful features from medical images and clinical data.CNN are specifically effective in medical images, making them ideal for detecting lung nodules and classify them as benign or malingnant.ResNet ,which deep learning further enhances classification accuracy by using convolutional layers.SVM is widely used for classification task due to its effectiveness in handling small datasets and high-dimensional spaces.Among them, ResNet50 achieved the highest accuracy of 91.3%, making it the most effective for multi-class classification (Normal, Benign, Malignant).CNN followed with 85.6%, while RF and SVM achieved 84.4% and 83.2% respectively.

title: Bongo Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Nature-inspired Metaheuristic Approach for Efficient Optimization
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms have attracted much attention in recent years due to their ability to solve complex optimization problems.However, striking a good balance between exploration and exploitation remains a major challenge in designing these algorithms.In this paper, a new algorithm, the Bongo Optimization Algorithm (BOA), is introduced, which is inspired by the natural behavior of Bongo in searching for food resources and selecting highquality resources.In BOA, the behavior of Bongo's extensive movement in the habitat to explore different areas is used as the basis for designing the exploration phase, while the behavior of selective browsing of high-quality food is used to focus on promising areas and improve existing solutions, which forms the basis for the exploitation phase.This structure allows for an effective balance between global search and local refinement.In order to evaluate the performance of BOA, a set of 23 standard benchmark functions including unimodal test functions (F1-F7), highdimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13), and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23) has been investigated.The performance of BOA has been compared with 9 well-known metaheuristic algorithms and the statistical measures of mean, standard deviation (std), and rank have been used to analyze the results.In addition, the search behavior of BOA has been investigated through visual analysis, convergence curve, population diversity, exploration, and exploitation percentage.The simulation results show that BOA has obtained the first-best optimizer rank in all 23 benchmark functions F1-F23 and has provided 100% successful and competitive performance compared to the investigated algorithms.Also, the analyses have confirmed the ability of BOA to maintain appropriate diversity in the early stages and increase exploitation in the final stages of optimization.The findings of this study show that BOA has been introduced as a powerful metaheuristic optimizer with high power in balancing exploration and exploitation and has the potential to be used in a wide range of optimization problems in science and real-world applications.Future studies can focus on developing multi-objective, binary versions and applying BOA to complex engineering problems.

title: Subvacuum jamming for secure communication
abstract: Artificial-noise jamming improves physical-layer security by degrading an eavesdropper's channel, but the injected noise also interferes with the legitimate receiver. We introduce a correlated-jamming protocol based on classical and quantum correlations that suppresses this self-interference while preserving the jamming penalty experienced by the eavesdropper. Bob broadcasts one mode of a correlated two-mode source and retains the second as a local reference. Eve, who has no access to the retained mode, receives the full thermal jamming field, whereas Bob uses an optimized joint measurement to cancel its correlated fluctuations. The residual self-jamming noise is governed by the conditional variance of the transmitted jamming quadrature given the retained reference. Any classically correlated source is bounded by the vacuum-noise floor and therefore restores Bob, at best, to his unjammed receiver noise. An entangled two-mode squeezed source surpasses this limit and produces sub-vacuum residual noise, with the maximum quantum advantage set by the transmissivity of the jamming path back to Bob. In the bright-source regime, this advantage becomes a fixed reduction in Bob's noise floor, independent of the signal and jamming powers. Within a bounded-collection wiretap model, correlated jamming preserves positive secrecy even when Eve has a stronger direct channel than Bob and remains effective against collective measurements on Eve's Gaussian output states. The protocol supports bright classical message transmission and requires no end-to-end quantum channel. Possible applications include shot-noise-limited optical communication, cryogenic microwave networks, and covert or power-constrained secure links.

Eve, who has no access to the retained mode, receives the full thermal jamming field, whereas Bob uses an optimized joint measurement to cancel its correlated fluctuations. The residual self-jamming noise is governed by the conditional variance of the transmitted jamming quadrature given the retained reference. Any classically correlated source is bounded by the vacuum-noise floor and therefore restores Bob, at best, to his unjammed receiver noise. An entangled two-mode squeezed source surpasses this limit and produces sub-vacuum residual noise, with the maximum quantum advantage set by the transmissivity of the jamming path back to Bob. In the bright-source regime, this advantage becomes a fixed reduction in Bob's noise floor, independent of the signal and jamming powers. Within a bounded-collection wiretap model, correlated jamming preserves positive secrecy even when Eve has a stronger direct channel than Bob and remains effective against collective measurements on Eve's Gaussian output states. The protocol supports bright classical message transmission and requires no end-to-end quantum channel. Possible applications include shot-noise-limited optical communication, cryogenic microwave networks, and covert or power-constrained secure links.

title: Hidden Timers and Context Offsets in a Diffusion World Model of Ms. Pac-Man: Pre-registered Tests and Replications
abstract: Pixel diffusion world models predict the next frame from a few past frames, so they cannot see state the screen does not show. We study a hidden timer in a DIAMOND-style model of Ms. Pac-Man, whose ghosts wait in a pen for up to 91 steps with no on-screen countdown. Models that see only their last 4 or 8 frames park the ghosts: in 450-step rollouts on held-out episodes, 16-23 of 30 rollouts keep the pen occupied for 200+ steps, against none in the real game. A 10-frame context with a 97-step reach removes the parking (0 of 30; paired difference to 4 frames -0.57, 95% CI [-0.77, -0.37] over episodes), and a pre-registered second training seed reproduces this. We propose a context-offset hypothesis: a model can time a hidden event of period N only as precisely as its context offsets resolve -N. A pre-registered sweep of 23 small models on a synthetic game, scored against an ideal observer with the same offsets, supports it in part: no model times a period beyond its reach, a frame exactly N steps back gives observer-level timing at three of four long periods, and one period between two frames parks. Moving a single frame from -81 to -80 takes that model from parking in 37 of 60 starts to none, in the original run and four further training seeds. Several registered tests failed, among them the replication's second stage, a second real game, a DIAMOND prediction and two latent-action models; all are reported. title: E8 Root Lattice as Universal Topological Quantum Error-Correcting Code — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240-dimensional E8 root lattice, when interpreted as stabilizer generators with Fibonacci-scaled syndrome weights at 132Hz, forms a universal topological quantum error-correcting code whose code distance scales with the golden ratio φ across the 8-dimensional Cartan substructure. The 120 Cartan conjugate pairs provide symmetric encoding subspaces while φ-modulated resonance at 132Hz determines syndrome extraction intervals, achieving logical qubit protection against both phase and bit-flip errors. This geometrically grounded error correction mechanism explains the decoherence suppression observed in the resonance framework, as the E8 lattice's optimal sphere-packing property guarantees maximal separation between logical codewords. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Connectivity optimization of artificial neural network with evolutionary computation algorithms
abstract: Human intelligence has historically produced various solutions to the challenges it has faced thanks to its cognitive abilities such as learning, remembering, comparing, and problem-solving. One of the most fundamental examples of artificial intelligence approaches that emerged by modeling these behaviors specific to intelligence is the artificial neural network (ANN), inspired by the biological nervous system. ANNs, with their similarity to biological nervous systems, present a highly complex system, and with technological advancements, the modeling and applicability of these systems are constantly increasing. In this study, a new ANN architecture inspired by the biological nervous system was designed. To improve the classification performance of the developed architecture, the connections in the network were treated as a binary optimization problem and optimized using the Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) algorithm. Following the architecture design, the weights of the connections in the network were optimized using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm which works with continuous values. As a result, a network architecture compatible with the biological nervous system, flexible in structure, and highly applicable to various problem types was created. The developed method was tested on Breast Cancer, Hepatitis, Mammographic Mass and Haberman’s Survival datasets. Additionally, proposed model compared with the Genetic Algorithm (GA), one of the most widely used evolutionary computation methods in the literature for connection optimization. Specifically, the proposed model reduces the input layer size from 5 to 2 in the Mammographic Mass domain by applying aggressive feature selection. It successfully reduces computational complexity by eliminating up to 12 hidden neurons in the Hepatitis dataset without sacrificing classification accuracy, thus providing significant structural pruning. Furthermore, it demonstrates high stability across all metrics with minimal standard deviation, proving that the synergy between binary and continuous swarm variants generates highly concise, lightweight, and efficient neural network topologies

title: Interpretable Dynamic Graph Learning via Dual‐Granularity Large Language Model Alignment
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic graph‐level embedding aims to learn whole‐graph representations from temporal snapshots. Existing methods predominantly follow a single‐vector paradigm that encodes each snapshot as a continuous latent vector, suffering from two key limitations: (1) Stage–Snapshot Entanglement, where within‐stage fluctuations and cross‐stage transitions are conflated without explicit granularity distinction; and (2) Implicit Structural Semantics, where meaningful structural properties remain buried in latent coordinates and are never exposed as interpretable, language‐compatible units. To address these issues, we propose DyGLLM, an LLM‐compatible framework that constructs and aligns dual‐granularity structural representations for dynamic graph understanding. Specifically, DyGLLM maps temporally coherent evolution regimes into selective structural tokens , providing explicit stage‐level anchors in the LLM token space. It further constructs graph fingerprints to verbalize each snapshot's prototype deviation, temporal variation and topological profile into language‐readable structural descriptions. A hybrid structure QA alignment mechanism with LoRA fine‐tuning is then introduced to align structural tokens and graph fingerprints with the LLM's representation space, enabling the model to interpret and reason over explicit structural contexts. Extensive experiments on five dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate that DyGLLM achieves consistently competitive performance across graph similarity ranking, temporal anomaly detection and change point detection, validating the effectiveness of the proposed dual‐granularity structural representation.

title: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
abstract: The rise of autonomous AI agents represents a major paradigm shift in how users interact with mobile devices. Frameworks such as MobileRun and Mobile-Use can autonomously navigate Android applications and execute complex multi-step tasks. To interpret user interfaces, these frameworks rely primarily on Android accessibility (A11y) trees and secondarily on visual screenshots. In this paper, we demonstrate that this architectural dependence on unsanitized accessibility metadata, together with visual input, introduces a systemic vulnerability to indirect prompt injection. We show that adversarial prompts can cause autonomous agents to abandon their original objectives, violate context boundaries, and perform unauthorized device actions. Our empirical evaluation demonstrates goal hijacking, context drift, and unauthorized actions across visually hidden and fully exposed attack scenarios. In aggregate, MobileRun reaches an attack success rate of 0.822 with Gemma4:31B, while Mobile-Use with Qwen3.6:35B reduces this to 0.150 but does not eliminate context drift or unauthorized actions. These findings reveal that current mobile agent frameworks fail to enforce semantic context boundaries, treating passive environmental text as trusted instructions. Finally, we present a taxonomy of these attacks and discuss the need for zero-trust input validation, dedicated security agents, and strict context isolation within mobile agent architectures.

title: INTERPRETING RANKING MODELS: FROM FEATURE ATTRIBUTIONS TO MECHANISTIC COMPREHENSION
abstract: The rapid adoption of Neural Ranking Models (NRMs) in Information Retrieval (IR) underscores the urgent need for robust interpretability methods to ensure their reliability and transparency. Despite their widespread use, how NRMs model query-document relevance remains poorly understood, limiting their application in high-stakes domains. This dissertation addresses this gap by developing generalizable, scalable, and theoretically grounded interpretability methods for ranking systems, spanning both post-hoc feature attribution and mechanistic analysis of internal model structure. First, we extend the Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) framework to NRMs, proposing RankLIME. This framework is able to generate local feature attributions for pointwise, pairwise, as well as listwise ranking models. Using RankLIME, practitioners gain a scalable tool to interpret the individual contributions of features to the ranking decisions of complex neural models. Next, recognizing the inconsistencies and contradictions in existing empirical ranking feature attribution methods, we adopt an axiomatic approach, establishing a set of fundamental principles that ranking-based attribution methods should satisfy. To this end, we introduce the RankSHAP framework, using the Shapley value from cooperative game theory. RankSHAP ensures that feature attributions are generalizable, consistent, and aligned with human intuition. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and diverse ranking models, coupled with a user study, validate the effectiveness of RankSHAP. An axiomatic analysis further clarifies the compliance and deviations of other attribution methods relative to the proposed axioms, enhancing our understanding of their reliability. Beyond feature attributions, this dissertation delves into the internal mechanisms of transformer-based ranking LLMs to understand the abstract features these models internally encode to model relevance in ranking decisions. Through a layer-wise analysis of LLM neuron activations, we investigate whether known statistical and human-engineered features—such as term frequency, inverse document frequency, and covered query term ratio—are embedded within network representations across different LLM configurations. These findings provide insights into the internal workings of ranking LLMs, laying the groundwork for designing more transparent and effective ranking systems. This dissertation further advances mechanistic interpretability by introducing a coalitional framework for studying how neurons cooperate within fine-tuned ranking LLMs. While prior analyses often treat neurons independently, empirical evidence suggests that task-specific features in LoRA-tuned models emerge through interactions among groups of neurons, particularly in mid-layer MLP blocks. To capture this structure, the dissertation models neurons as agents in a hedonic game, where preferences are defined by their synergistic contributions to layer-local computations. Using top-responsive utilities and the PAC-Top-Cover algorithm, it identifies stable coalitions of neurons whose joint ablations produce non-additive effects, and tracks how these coalitions persist, split, merge, or disappear across layers. Applied to LLaMA, Mistral, and Pythia rerankers fine-tuned for scalar output tasks, this framework discovers coalitions with consistently higher synergy than clustering-based baselines. By revealing higher-order functional units beyond individual neurons, hedonic coalitions provide a new lens into how fine-tuned language models encode task-relevant features and computations. Taken together, these contributions connect feature attribution, axiomatic analysis, probing, and coalition-based mechanistic interpretability into a broader framework for understanding neural ranking systems. More broadly, they point toward an emerging research agenda for the community: building a systematic science of reverse-engineering large language models, with particular attention to the emergent features and statistical regularities encoded in their weights and internal computations, especially within MLP submodules. Advancing this agenda will require weight-based and mechanism-based interpretability methods capable of recovering the latent priors, abstractions, and invariances that models internalize during training. Such progress would not only deepen scientific understanding of how learning systems compress, organize, and represent knowledge, but also help extract actionable insights about the real-world phenomena these models capture. Ultimately, this dissertation contributes toward bridging interpretability and performance in neural ranking models, and toward a more principled foundation for transparent, accountable, and scientifically informative machine learning systems.

title: AI and Data-Driven Decision Making: Innovating Strategy in Modern Business Management
abstract: Advanced AI technologies and analytics inform critical decisions within contemporary corporate strategies. Existing research underscores the advantages of using artificial intelligence for operations and analysis but lacks comprehensive insights into how these systems affect overall strategy formulation, business flexibility, and leadership performance in various sectors. In pursuit of filling this void, our current research investigates how machine learning, predictive analysis, natural language handling, and automated systems contribute significantly to improving business strategies. This analysis explores how companies utilize vast amounts of information to predict changes in markets, enhance their processes, elevate service quality for customers, and secure an edge over rivals. Drawing upon examples from sectors like retail, health care, manufacturing, and finance, this document demonstrates how artificial intelligence enhances business strategies through real-world applications. Additionally, this research examines significant obstacles including issues related to personal information security, discrimination in machine learning models, moral considerations, and the necessity of efficient cooperation between humans and artificial intelligence systems. Evidence highlights the significance of cultivating data-centric environments, enhancing technological frameworks, and nurturing leaders adept at guiding AI-informed organizational shifts. In summary, this study offers a comprehensive view of how artificial intelligence and digital ecosystems facilitate agile, robust, and insightful approaches within evolving corporate landscapes.

title: Learning Structure to Support Autonomous Control Decisions
abstract: Autonomous systems have been the subject of substantial consequential research, with applications ranging from space exploration to self-driving vehicles. In unstructured and novel environments, such systems must make control decisions under partial observability, where sensing is noisy and incomplete and dynamics are uncertain or imperfectly modeled. Issues stemming from partial observability and uncertainty can be mitigated using predictive models that summarize an agent's past experiences; that is, mechanisms capable of anticipating the outcomes of the agent's (or even other agents') decisions and actions. This dissertation develops exploration methods for learning transition models of controllable interactions between a robot and its environment and evaluates how these learned models improve planning under uncertainty. Such planning capabilities, in turn, support agents in sequential decision making, as well as in active information gathering purposes aimed at reducing uncertainty while reaching desirable states and avoiding unrecoverable failures. This dissertation specifically investigates the challenge of learning a model of an agent's transition function, which encodes a probability distribution over outcome states that may occur when an action is performed at a given state. These models support agents in reasoning over trajectories of (open or closed loop) controlled state transitions in order to solve various types of tasks. Furthermore, we study mechanisms to learn such models through autonomous exploration in a way that addresses issues of exploration efficiency, ability of learned models to solve downstream tasks, accuracy of models in describing dynamics, and completeness of models in fully representing entire state-action spaces. We introduce two novel methods for autonomously exploring partially observable environments in order to efficiently build predictive models. These exploration processes leverage information theoretic measures that capture model-learning progress based on how much dynamics model estimates change during interaction. We also investigate various metrics to quantify these changes, such as the magnitude of entropy change and the Kullback-Leibler divergence between successive model estimates. The first algorithm we propose, Intrinsically Motivated Structure Learning, greedily maximizes learning progress and thereby efficiently guides exploration toward actions where the estimated transition model does not match reality. The second algorithm, Acquisition of Salient Control Knowledge, identifies effective exploration and information gathering behaviors by planning over a fixed horizon and leveraging currently estimated models to balance exploration and exploitation, thereby enabling more rapid construction of accurate and complete predictive models. We show that these algorithms converge to stable and accurate model estimates using fewer actions than baseline approaches. We then evaluate the impact of the learned models by quantifying the quality and performance of autonomous agent behaviors when solving novel tasks through model-based planning in belief space. The tasks in which we evaluate our techniques represent settings in which an agent faces incomplete information and must actively select actions to mitigate uncertainty by using its models. We show that models learned through our methods support decision making that actively reduces uncertainty and enables agents to solve families of tasks with fewer actions and higher success rates than existing techniques.

The tasks in which we evaluate our techniques represent settings in which an agent faces incomplete information and must actively select actions to mitigate uncertainty by using its models. We show that models learned through our methods support decision making that actively reduces uncertainty and enables agents to solve families of tasks with fewer actions and higher success rates than existing techniques.

title: What a Secret Rotation Buys: Exact Retrieval and Measured Leakage in Vector Databases
abstract: Vector databases require embedding geometry for similarity search, but that geometry can also support inference. We evaluate keyed orthogonal obfuscation against a snapshot adversary. The practical Walsh–Hadamard construction has no established confidentiality guarantee; its empirical evaluation covers only the tested attacks. For Haar-uniform maps, the Gram matrix exactly characterizes a reused-key corpus view, whereas it is only a leakage lower bound for the structured implementation. Across three BEIR datasets, three encoders and 2029 queries, exhaustive clear/transformed top-10 sets agree in all nine configurations. Five of six containerized engines also return identical sets; the sixth exhibits comparable re-indexing variability. Median client transform latency is 0.032–0.042 ms. Known rank-sufficient pairs recover the map. Without matched records, same-distribution auxiliary embeddings support median four-way topic accuracies of 0.833, 0.808 and 0.869 in the primary experiment. A paired evaluation over five shared-label mixtures and 30 trials per encoder shows that public-distribution shift reduces assigned-label accuracy, while evaluator-only label reassignment and normalized mutual information reveal residual topic structure. Noise-padding findings are restricted to four estimators on SciFact/MiniLM at one corpus size. These results characterize exact similarity preservation and measured leakage, not encryption or general semantic confidentiality.

title: Observation Window Design Outweighs Architectural Complexity in Deep Learning for Sepsis Mortality Prediction
abstract: Deep learning models for predicting sepsis mortality often obscure which design choices genuinely improve performance.We developed a sequential model using 19,902 Sepsis-3 patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV), processing hourly physiological sequences via convolutional and bidirectional recurrent layers alongside static patient features.Under matched conditions, sliding-window augmentation improved discrimination by 0.033 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), of which repeated training examples accounted for the larger share.The static feature pathway contributed 0.061, whereas the convolutional block had no measurable effect.On a held-out test set the model reached an AUROC of 0.902; gradient boosting, a bidirectional long short-term memory network, and a Transformer encoder reached 0.865, 0.855, and 0.851 under an identical protocol and tuning budget.When all features were restricted to the information available at each prediction time, discrimination fell to 0.807 at six hours and 0.839 at twelve, so shorter horizons carry a substantial cost.These results suggest that in this task, input representation and observation length mattered more than architectural complexity.

title: Web Interactive Content Filtering Model Integrating Prompt Classifier and Intent Understanding
abstract: To accurately identify and intercept harmful content generated in user interactions on Web platforms such as social media and online forums, this study proposes a Web interactive content filtering model that integrates Prompt classifiers and intent understanding. The model adopts a hierarchical review architecture with dual-module collaboration. The front-end deploys a Prompt classifier based on Deep Contrastive Learning (DCL), and uses the attention mechanism and deep convolutional network to perform rapid semantic analysis and preliminary screening of real-time comments and conversations. The back-end introduces an intent understanding module based on search-enhanced generation and Large Language Models (LLMs) to conduct in-depth contextual analysis of preliminary screening warning content to distinguish malicious attacks from legitimate sensitive topic discussions. Experiments showed that the system performed well on a test set containing 52,397 Chinese Web interactive texts. The Prompt classifier module achieved a precision of 95.2% and a recall of 96.5%. After collaborative calibration with the intent understanding module, the false alarm rate of the system was significantly reduced to 4.4%, while the recall rate remained at 96.1%. From the results, this study provides a content security solution for Web interactive scenarios that combines high accuracy, strong semantic understanding capabilities, and real-time response performance. It can effectively purify the cyberspace environment while ensuring freedom of interaction, with important practical application value.
