title: Differentially Private Statistical Learning: Uncertainty Estimation and Utility Preservation
abstract: Organizations increasingly rely on sensitive data for high-impact decisions, making it essential to develop methods that ensure individual privacy while preserving the utility of downstream analyses. Differential privacy (DP) has emerged as the gold standard for such guarantees. This thesis contributes novel methods for differentially private statistical learning, with a focus on improving the usability of private inference through rigorous uncertainty quantification and the accuracy of private estimators via data-dependent mechanisms. First, we develop parametric bootstrap methods for DP confidence intervals, enabling uncertainty estimation through post-processing while accounting for both sampling and privacy noise. This approach avoids multiple accesses to the data and remains accurate even in small-sample regimes. Second, we propose data-dependent sufficient statistic perturbation, a framework that applies private query-answering algorithms to release sufficient statistics, improving estimation in both linear and logistic regression. Third, we introduce a data-dependent method for private multivariate Gaussian covariance estimation: instead of perturbing the entire matrix, we iteratively select the most informative covariance entries to measure under the privacy budget, then reconstruct the full positive semidefinite matrix via a maximum-entropy completion. By concentrating noise where it matters most, we show that this strategy yields high-utility covariance estimates, paving the way for novel continuous synthetic data generation methods. These contributions aim to bridge theory and practice, advancing the applicability of differential privacy in statistical machine learning.

title: Enterprise Agentic AI Reference Architecture
abstract: Agentic AI extends Generative AI from response generation to goal-oriented digital execution. Enterprise agents can interpret objectives, plan tasks, retrieve knowledge, invoke tools, call APIs, maintain memory, coordinate with other agents, and adapt execution based on intermediate results. These capabilities require a reference architecture that separates probabilistic reasoning from deterministic enterprise controls. This paper proposes an Enterprise Agentic AI Reference Architecture spanning experience, agent orchestration, planning and reasoning, enterprise knowledge, memory, model runtime, tool and integration services, identity, policy enforcement, observability, security, Responsible AI, and human oversight. The architecture integrates SAP Business Technology Platform, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, SAP HANA Cloud, SAP Integration Suite, enterprise APIs, RAG, Knowledge Graphs, and cloud-native services. It provides patterns for secure and scalable agent deployment across hybrid and multi-cloud environments while preserving accountability, bounded autonomy, operational resilience, and business value.

title: Enterprise Multi-Agent Architecture Framework
abstract: Enterprises are rapidly moving from isolated copilots toward ecosystems of specialized AI agents that collaborate across business processes, data domains, applications, and cloud platforms. Multi-agent systems can improve decomposition, parallel execution, specialization, resilience, and decision quality, but they also introduce architectural challenges involving identity, delegation, shared memory, tool access, message routing, conflict resolution, security, observability, and accountability. This paper proposes an Enterprise Multi-Agent Architecture Framework that defines a layered architecture for agent discovery, orchestration, inter-agent communication, knowledge grounding, enterprise integration, policy enforcement, runtime isolation, and human oversight. The framework combines enterprise architecture principles, Zero Trust, Responsible AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Knowledge Graphs, API governance, event-driven integration, and lifecycle management. It enables organizations to design scalable multi-agent environments in which specialized agents can collaborate safely while maintaining traceability, bounded authority, data protection, and measurable business outcomes across hybrid and multi-cloud landscapes.

title: Closing the Productive Half of Cross-Language Conversation: An Anticipatory Multilingual Conversation Assistance System for Wearable Devices
abstract: Cross-language conversation support technology has advanced almost exclusively on the receptive side: translation devices and subtitle glasses help a user understand an interlocutor, but leave the user unaided at the moment of formulating a reply in the interlocutor's language. This paper presents a wearable conversation assistance system that closes this productive half of the loop. Worn by only one party to the conversation, the system (1) captures the interlocutor's speech and projects real-time translated subtitles onto a near-eye display; (2) anticipatorily generates, in parallel with the interlocutor's ongoing turn and drawing on streaming partial speech-recognition hypotheses, dialogue history, and a persistent user profile, a small ranked set of candidate responses in the interlocutor's language, presented with spoken pronunciation guidance delivered by in-ear text-to-speech; and (3) provides a free-expression fallback in which the wearer speaks once in their native language and reads aloud the projected translation. The central mechanism is latency concealment through anticipation: because candidate generation overlaps the interlocutor's turn, large-language-model inference time is absorbed within the natural duration of speech and the turn-taking gap, so candidates are ready before the wearer's turn begins. The paper describes the three-tier architecture (smart glasses, paired mobile device, cloud services), the three-step conversation loop, the functional design of candidate ranking and selection — including silent gesture-based selection that keeps the interaction invisible to the interlocutor — and the user-profile and privacy model. The system is described as disclosed in U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 64/170,246; performance figures cited are the design targets stated in that disclosure, not production measurements.

title: Extending the Isabelle Insider and Infrastructure Framework Using Generative AI for Refining Refinements
abstract: Abstract The Isabelle Insider and Infrastructure framework (IIIf) supports formal security engineering by using attack trees to identify attacks that lead to security improvements by refinement. Based on the interactive theorem prover Isabelle, the framework combines mathematical rigor with automation for interactive proofs. However, this process is highly complex and applying it to realistic case study is challenging in terms of time and expert knowledge. Integrating generative AI into this process of formal security engineering appears inevitable. In this paper, we illustrate the IIIf on summarizing and improving a previous case study of the Corona Warning App (CWA). This provides a relevant basis for using Claude Code as a proof-copilot for IIIf refinements. We derive an alternative refinement for CWA that represents a more realistic solution. Based on this experience, we extract rules and heuristics for proof-copiloting of security engineering in IIIf and define valid refinement contexts.

title: Compact Reinforcement Learning: Resource-Efficient Formulations for Large-Scale Decision Making
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a general framework for addressing problems involving sequential decision-making. However, modern practical applications of RL involve prohibitively large state and action sets: such as those in slate recommendations, image-based control, and large language-modeling tasks. Standard formulations of these problems demand intractable amounts of data and computational resources. Achieving high performance without incurring high resource costs requires compact problem formulations that capture task-relevant information while abstracting away the rest. This thesis develops and analyzes such compact formulations for decision-making problems characterized by large action and large state sets, as well as the corresponding challenge of obtaining reward feedback over them. We first address the challenge of large action sets encountered in off-policy evaluation (OPE) for slate recommendations. Risk-sensitive metrics (such as quantiles and CVaR), common for evaluating performance in this setting, require estimation of the full performance distribution from logged data rather than just the expected performance. This requires distributional OPE, which in this high-dimensional setting is highly sample-inefficient and suffers from high variance. We introduce a low-variance variant of the standard estimator that approximates the joint influence of all action dimensions through a simpler combination of marginal effects, and establish conditions under which the resulting estimator remains unbiased. Empirical evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate that even when these conditions are not strictly satisfied, the proposed method outperforms more general baselines. We next focus on large state spaces and long-horizon problems, where classical OPE methods become intractable or error-prone. We develop a framework that combines state abstraction with a model-learning approach that distills complex, potentially continuous problems into compact, discrete models called abstract reward processes (ARPs), which preserve sufficient information about policy performance. Within the proposed OPE framework, these ARPs are estimated from off-policy data and we prove that their predictions are consistent. Varying the granularity of the state abstraction function reveals a broad range of previously unexplored hybrid ARP-based OPE estimators, encompassing classical methods as the limiting cases. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that estimators within this framework outperform existing OPE baselines across a variety of domains. Finally, we study the problem of reward selection under limited feedback constraints in reinforcement learning. While large amounts of state transition data can often be collected or generated cheaply in modern applications, obtaining reward feedback is practically expensive, particularly when relying on human feedback, over large state and action sets. In such cases, when RL is constrained to operating with limited or partial reward feedback, a central question arises: which subset of data should be reward-labeled to maximize policy performance? We formalize this reward selection problem and empirically investigate several sampling-based selection strategies, aiming to identify selection patterns that generalize across domains and enable more efficient use of reward feedback. Our results show that effective selection strategies can achieve performance comparable to learning from a fully labeled dataset while reward-labeling only a small fraction of the data, enabling feedback-efficient reinforcement learning in large-scale resource-constrained problems.

title: SAP AI Core Enterprise Reference Architecture
abstract: SAP AI Core provides enterprise capabilities for executing, managing, and operationalizing Artificial Intelligence workloads within SAP Business Technology Platform landscapes. Enterprise adoption requires a reference architecture that connects model runtime, data, applications, identity, security, integration, observability, Responsible AI, and lifecycle governance. This paper proposes a SAP AI Core Enterprise Reference Architecture spanning user and application channels, AI service orchestration, model runtime, data and feature access, SAP HANA Cloud, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, SAP Integration Suite, model repositories, security controls, monitoring, and governance. The architecture supports predictive AI, custom machine learning, Generative AI, embeddings, and agentic services while maintaining clean-core integration, least privilege, auditability, resilience, and business accountability. It also defines implementation patterns, deployment controls, model lifecycle processes, and operational KPIs/KRIs. The proposed architecture enables organizations to scale AI on SAP BTP in a secure, reusable, and governed manner.

title: New results on the quantum security analysis of lightweight block cipher Simeck
abstract: Abstract Simeck demonstrates reliable resistance against conventional cryptanalytic attacks and offers sound security properties, making it a noteworthy design in the field of lightweight cryptography. Nevertheless, ongoing progress in quantum computing poses a potential threat to the security of Simeck, underscoring the need for a rigorous analysis of its quantum resilience. In this paper, we analyze quantum distinguishers and key-recovery attacks on Simeck in the Q2 model. Leveraging the connection between truncated differentials and periodic functions, we revisit Simon-type qCPA distinguishers for Simeck-32/48/64 and further extend them to the qCCA setting. The qCPA distinguishers cover 8/9/11 rounds of Simeck-32/48/64, matching the round numbers reported by Lu et al. (2026), whereas our qCCA distinguishers cover 10/11/13 rounds. Based on these distinguishers, we investigate their application to Grover-meets-Simon key-recovery attacks on reduced-round Simeck. Furthermore, we mount qCPA key-recovery attacks on 11/12/14-round Simeck-32/48/64 and extend them to qCCA attacks on 13/14/16-round Simeck-32/48/64. Finally, we provide empirical estimates of the quantum resources required for the proposed key-recovery attacks. For Simeck-32/48/64, the empirical quantum query complexities are $$2^{28.09}/2^{40.32}/2^{52.59}$$ 2 28.09 / 2 40.32 / 2 52.59 in the qCPA setting and $$2^{26.81}/2^{39}/2^{51.17}$$ 2 26.81 / 2 39 / 2 51.17 in the qCCA setting, respectively, under the stated decision-test assumptions and empirical false-positive estimates.

Furthermore, we mount qCPA key-recovery attacks on 11/12/14-round Simeck-32/48/64 and extend them to qCCA attacks on 13/14/16-round Simeck-32/48/64. Finally, we provide empirical estimates of the quantum resources required for the proposed key-recovery attacks. For Simeck-32/48/64, the empirical quantum query complexities are $$2^{28.09}/2^{40.32}/2^{52.59}$$ 2 28.09 / 2 40.32 / 2 52.59 in the qCPA setting and $$2^{26.81}/2^{39}/2^{51.17}$$ 2 26.81 / 2 39 / 2 51.17 in the qCCA setting, respectively, under the stated decision-test assumptions and empirical false-positive estimates.

title: STIR: Reed–Solomon Proximity Testing with Fewer Queries
abstract: We present STIR (Shift To Improve Rate), an interactive oracle proof of proximity (IOPP) for Reed–Solomon codes that achieves the best known query complexity of any concretely efficient IOPP for this problem. For λ bits of security, STIR has query complexity O (log d + λ · log logd ), while FRI, a popular protocol, has query complexity O ( λ · log d ) (including variants of FRI based on conjectured security assumptions). STIR relies on a new technique for recursively improving the rate of the tested Reed–Solomon code. We provide an implementation of STIR compiled to a SNARK. Compared to a highly-optimized implementation of FRI, STIR achieves an improvement in argument size that ranges from 1.25 × to 2.46 × depending on the chosen parameters, with similar prover and verifier running times. For example, in order to achieve 128 bits of security for degree 2 26 and rate 1/4, STIR has argument size 114 KiB, compared to 211 KiB for FRI.

title: Towards Realistic Simulated Students: Aligning Language Models with Student Knowledge and Behavior
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in education, there is a growing need to quickly verify and steer LLM-generated content for the benefit of students. In particular, it is important to ensure that educational AI systems improve learning outcomes and engagement while minimizing potential harms. While it is possible to test new systems and content on real students, this process can be slow, costly, and insecure. Instead, simulated students, i.e., LLM-based models that mimic student behavior, can be used to quickly and safely verify AI systems. However, LLMs do not typically behave like real students, often exhibiting unrealistic behavioral patterns and knowledge trends, limiting how useful they can be. In this thesis, I address this problem by introducing multiple approaches for aligning LLMs with student behavior and knowledge. I further demonstrate how simulated students can be leveraged to align educational content with student-centered goals. First, I detail SMART, a method for fine-tuning LLMs with reinforcement learning (RL) that aligns the models with realistic response patterns based on student ability and question difficulty, deriving a reward function from item response theory. I demonstrate how LLMs trained with SMART can be used to reliably estimate question difficulty. Second, I introduce dialogue knowledge tracing (KT), where tutor-student dialogues are viewed as sequences of formative assessments, allowing the use of KT to model student knowledge in dialogues. I also detail LLMKT, an LLM-based method for estimating student knowledge that improves on prior KT approaches. Third, I detail a method for leveraging student models in LLM-based tutor training, where I use an RL pipeline that rewards tutor responses that result in better student learning outcomes, which are estimated using LLMKT. Fourth, I detail an evaluation framework that measures the realism of student simulations along multiple behavioral, cognitive, and linguistic dimensions, facilitating the development of more aligned simulated student methods in the future. Finally, I conclude by detailing future directions for improving and broadening simulated students methods, and for leveraging simulated students to tackle current challenges in education.

title: NV magnetic-localisation benchmarks
abstract: Software and analysis data accompanying Beyond Parameter Counts: Standardisation, Nested Model Selection, and Inference Backends in Neural Regression for NV Magnetic Localisation. This deposit preserves GitHub release v1.0.0, commit dd480273015d9fd313de51c8cbb63dc1174c4291. The analyses cover the Weng NV-array localisation task, input and target standardisation, nested leave-one-acquisition-out compact-model selection, the independent Meneses elevator-localisation task, and CPU inference measurements with PyTorch, NumPy and ONNX Runtime. The source archive contains the 372 files tracked in the GitHub release. The results archive supplies the two large prediction tables. title: Geological Reliability in Deep Learning Mineral Prospectivity Mapping: A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) has rapidly advanced through the integration of deep learning, multisource geoscience data, and increasingly complex representation-learning approaches. However, the reliability of AI-derived prospectivity predictions remains a critical challenge because high predictive performance does not necessarily indicate geological validity, spatial transferability, or exploration usefulness. The key challenge is therefore not model complexity, but aligning geological knowledge, data representation, validation, and uncertainty assessment to ensure reliable interpretation. This review provides a structured critical synthesis of geological reliability in deep learning-based MPM, focusing on the methodological factors that influence whether AI outputs can support defensible exploration decisions. Rather than comparing algorithms solely by predictive accuracy, we examine the interconnected roles of geological representation, prediction support, label construction, negative-sample strategies, validation design, uncertainty quantification, explainability, transferability, and independent geological verification. Assessment of representative AI-based MPM studies reveals inconsistent reporting of these reliability dimensions, limiting reproducibility and meaningful comparison across studies. The review identifies recurring reliability bottlenecks, including spatial leakage caused by inappropriate validation strategies, uncertainty introduced during evidence-layer construction, ambiguity associated with unlabelled geological regions, and limitations in interpreting model explanations as geological causality. To organize these challenges, we propose a hierarchical evidence framework consisting of eight levels: methodological feasibility, internally validated predictive performance, spatial or temporal transferability, geological coherence, calibrated uncertainty, independent geological evidence, prospective field or drilling evidence, and demonstrated decision value. This framework clarifies the strength of claims that can be supported by different levels of evidence and provides a basis for transparent reporting and reliability assessment. Future progress in AI-based MPM will require integration of predictive capability with geological knowledge, robust validation, uncertainty-aware modelling, interpretable predictions, and independent geological verification. The proposed framework aims to support the development of more reproducible, transferable, and decision-relevant AI-assisted mineral exploration workflows.

title: Beyond Binary Rewrite Decisions: Separating Rewrite-Intensity Control from Level Prediction in a Frozen-LLM Generation-and-Selection Pipeline for Korean Easy-Read Drafting
abstract: Editors of published Korean Easy-Read documents changed 50 aligned sentences by widely varying amounts (edit distance 0.39–0.89), motivating rewrite intensity as a control variable for large language models (LLMs). We ask whether a requested intensity is realized per sentence and whether the level to request can be predicted from the source, using a generation-and-selection pipeline over a frozen LLM (EXAONE-3.5-7.8B-Instruct) in two sequential protocols with criteria hash-frozen before generation. Realized intensity is normalized character edit distance, which measures change, not readability, meaning preservation or Easy-Read quality. A four-level protocol (v1) ordered outputs on average but failed the sentence-level criterion (14/50 under its zero-tolerance rule). A three-level follow-up (v2), designed after that failure with several simultaneous changes, met its criterion for the whole pipeline, including its intensity-aware selector: 41/50 sources were non-decreasingly ordered at the declared tolerance (24/50 with strict increases; post hoc, 30/50 without the selector’s intensity-match term at that tolerance). Three runs of one LLM proxy perceived the ordering (consistency, not validity); no human evaluated the outputs. Stronger levels reduced source similarity without monotonically reducing lexical difficulty. Six source features did not support prediction of the LLM-proxy-preferred level under a pre-specified rule (quadratic-weighted κ −0.098 vs. 0.012), so no adaptive allocation was built. Rewrite-intensity control and level allocation therefore require separate validation.

title: Advancing End-to-End Privacy in Machine Learning: Input, Output, and Beyond
abstract: As machine learning is increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications, ensuring strong privacy guarantees while maintaining accuracy and efficiency remains a fundamental challenge. Privacy-enhancing technologies, such as differential privacy (DP) and secure computation, provide rigorous protections, but their direct application often incurs significant tradeoffs that limit practical adoption. This dissertation advances the design of practical privacy-preserving machine learning systems by co-designing algorithms, model architectures, and cryptographic protocols to better balance privacy, accuracy, and efficiency. We begin by studying output privacy in machine learning. We introduce a DP mechanism for random forest classifiers based on a novel matrix representation that enables optimized noise allocation, significantly improving accuracy. We further examine the impact of DP mechanisms in real-world settings through a case study on Census data releases for redistricting, evaluating how privacy constraints affect downstream fairness validation. Next, we address input privacy by developing a secure protocol for fine-tuning language models using secure multiparty computation (MPC). To overcome numerical instability in MPC-based training, we propose an adaptive loss scaling technique that enables stable and efficient training of transformer-based models under secure computation constraints. Finally, we propose hybrid approaches that combine DP with cryptographic primitives to achieve both input and output privacy. Focusing on structured workloads such as counting queries, we selectively replace stronger cryptographic components with DP-aware ones, substantially reducing computational overhead while preserving the desired privacy guarantees.

title: Python's Indispensability in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: A Review
abstract: This review paper explores the vital role played by the programming language Python in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). It will discuss the origin of AI and ML, the first programming language used for it, and its bottlenecks will be made known. There will also be an exposition on the emergence of Python, its elements, and the comparison between Python and LISP. The adoption and integration of Python into AI and ML will be considered, and the advanced components of Python and their uses in AI and ML will also be discussed. The trajectory of AI and ML with Python and the game-changing benefits of using Python in AI and ML will be assessed. Suggestions will be given on what should be improved in Python to improve AI and ML.

title: Logical rationale and practical paths of digital-intelligence empowerment for improving health education literacy of college physical education teachers
abstract: With the continuous advancement of educational digitalization and health education in colleges and universities, new requirements have been put forward for the professional literacy of college physical education teachers. Based on relevant policy documents and existing studies, this paper analyzes the connotation, improvement logic, realistic adaptation and practical paths of digital-intelligence empowerment for the health education literacy of college physical education teachers. The study holds that this literacy can be understood from four dimensions: health knowledge integration, health information interpretation, health education transformation, and digital-intelligence application and ethics. Its improvement stems from the expansion of health education goals, the integration of physical education and health knowledge, and the collaboration between professional experience and data evidence. At present, there is still room for further improvement in the embedding of health education roles, the connection between physical education and health knowledge, the educational transformation of health data, and relevant support mechanisms. To this end, it is necessary to strengthen the professional role cognition oriented by health promotion, build a knowledge system integrating physical education and health, form a capability chain of "data acquisition – information interpretation – educational decision-making – teaching intervention – feedback adjustment", and improve the support mechanisms of training, teaching and research, interdisciplinary collaboration and evaluation.

title: Darwinian Gating with Goal-Reachable Branch Values: Foundation Alignment and Evidence under Stochastic Availability
abstract: We revise a fail-closed reasoning kernel by separating hard admissibility, goal reachability, counting entropy and stochastic continuation value. The earlier nine-coordinate potential and propagation product remain audited heuristics; neither follows from a physical free-energy law. Inspired by foundational work separating legal sectors, state counts, stochastic transitions and observable projection, we introduce a paper-local acyclic-graph adapter with an explicit goal-completion objective. For independently available edges revealed locally before choice, a sorted continuation backup is proved equivalent to stochastic Bellman optimization. On 600 fixed-seed synthetic graphs, expected completion increases from 57.22% for viability-filtered local ranking and 71.07% for best-path replanning to 73.34%. The paired gain over best-path replanning is 2.28 percentage points (95% interval 2.01–2.55). The new rule matches exact subset Bellman planning, and its advantage over viability disappears when all edges are available. A probability-shift diagnostic and independent Monte Carlo check are included. Earlier public-task and chronological forecasting controls remain parity results. The evidence supports continuation-aware selection under a declared stochastic graph model, not a new universal reasoning law, a CS-derived decision spectrum, or superiority over optimal planners.

title: Neural network optimization-based intelligent evaluation algorithm for international Chinese teaching effect
abstract: Evaluating the effectiveness of teaching Chinese as an international language is considered to be important within the context of global education; as such there is great difficulty in assessing whether or not the way it is delivered is effective due to variances in both learners and their respective learning environments. An intelligent evaluation algorithm based on neural network optimization to address teaching effectiveness problems is developed. The Chaotic Dragonfly Algorithm Optimized Multilayer Feed-Forward Neural Network (CDA-MFFNN) is implemented, to determine a higher level of prediction accuracy for effectiveness in teaching strategies. The data set used to train the CDA-MFFNN model is the Chinese Teaching Effectiveness Data Set, which contains 6,531 data records related to performance, engagement, and instructional attributes. Preprocessing involves min-max normalization and semantic coding of categorical variables, to reduce the number of dimensions and capture latent property patterns. While autoencoders are used as feature extraction method to capture latent patterns and reduce dimensionality. The MFFNN models the relationships between the processed features in a complex non-linear manner while the CDA optimizes the weights of the neural networks to improve convergence and prevent being stuck in local minima during training. Python-based experimental evaluation demonstrated a clear performance advantage over the baseline approaches, with the proposed method attaining 98.65% accuracy and a 98.20% F1-score. It also produced lower prediction errors, recording an MSE of 15.72 and an RMSE of 3.96. This research contributes to the development of intelligent educational analytics and provides action-oriented guidance for curriculum developers and policy makers. Not applicable.

title: The Impact of Retrieval Augmented Generation on the Reliability of Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable fluency but remain fundamentally unreliable for knowledge-intensive tasks due to hallucination, temporal staleness, and lack of verifiability.Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a dominant architectural paradigm that grounds generation in external evidence.This paper provides a comprehensive investigation into how RAG reshapes LLM reliability across factual accuracy, citation fidelity, temporal freshness, and robustness to noise.We benchmark five RAG variants against closed-book baselines using secondary datasets including Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and RGB.Results show an average 23.7% reduction in hallucination rate and 31.2%improvement in citation grounding when using advanced retrieval with self-reflection.However, we identify critical failure modes: retriever-generator misalignment, context distraction, and over-reliance on irrelevant passages.We propose a reliability framework and demonstrate that corrective and modular RAG designs significantly mitigate these risks.Our findings establish RAG as necessary but not sufficient for trustworthy deployment.

title: AI as a Catalyst for Purpose-Driven Business
abstract: Chapter 7 explores how artificial intelligence is transforming the architecture, culture and governance of modern organisations, revealing both the risks and opportunities of technological acceleration. It argues that AI does not simply automate existing processes but fundamentally reshapes how work is organised, how decisions are made and how value is created. Drawing on the author’s experience redesigning an advisory organisation at Human Planet, the chapter illustrates how AI can invert traditional hierarchical structures, replacing labour-intensive pyramids with lean, purpose-driven systems where experienced professionals are supported by intelligent tools. In this model, technology handles complexity and repetition, while humans focus on judgement, creativity and service. Beyond structural efficiency, the chapter examines the cultural and ethical implications of AI adoption. It highlights how intelligent systems can restore human-centred productivity by removing administrative burdens, enabling organisations to redirect energy towards meaning, collaboration and innovation. At the same time, the chapter warns that AI amplifies the values embedded in an organisation: when guided by vocation and ethical leadership, it strengthens transparency, accountability and stakeholder empowerment; when misaligned, it risks accelerating bias, opacity and institutional failure. Ultimately, Chapter 7 positions artificial intelligence not as a substitute for purpose but as a catalyst that makes organisational vocation more actionable, reinforcing the central premise of the vocating framework: that technology must serve human dignity, long-term stewardship and meaningful contribution.

title: Rethink‐ RAG : Dynamic Retrieval Decision and Cooperative Verification for Reliable Multi‐Hop Question Answering
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable multi‐hop question answering is important for knowledge‐intensive expert systems, where a wrong intermediate fact can propagate into an incorrect final decision. Existing Retrieval‐Augmented Generation (RAG) methods often retrieve for every sub‐question, even when the language model can answer a step from parametric knowledge, and this indiscriminate retrieval can introduce irrelevant or contradictory evidence. We propose Rethink‐RAG, a training‐free framework that combines dynamic retrieval decision with a cooperative answer verification pipeline. The dynamic retrieval decision module generates diverse rewrites of each sub‐question and applies majority voting to decide whether external retrieval is required. The cooperative verification pipeline then filters retrieved documents, quantifies support and opposition through token‐logit evidence, and arbitrates each candidate sub‐answer with an adaptive confidence threshold. Experiments on 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, and MuSiQueQA show that Rethink‐RAG improves answer reliability on knowledge‐intensive reasoning tasks, achieving 49.00% ACC on 2WikiMultihopQA and 49.60% ACC on HotpotQA with the Llama3‐8B evaluator. Additional revision experiments quantify the latency/API‐call trade‐off, sensitivity to the decision‐boundary factor, and the limitations observed on MuSiQueQA, giving a more complete view of the framework's practical operating range.

title: Temporal Correlations Reshape Causal Resources in Qubit Hamiltonian Recognition: Exact Two-Query Strategy Comparison and a Uniform Critical Crossover
abstract: We investigate binary recognition of an unknown qubit Hamiltonian using two queries of its evolution, with unknown evolution angles that are either independently resampled or shared with tunable temporal correlation. For a symmetric pair of nonorthogonal qubit Hamiltonians, we compare parallel (PAR), sequential (SEQ), and general (GEN) quantum strategies. An exact symmetry reduction expresses the sequential optimization through a three-dimensional correlation elliptope. A general-strategy dual certificate establishes the equality between optimal general and sequential strategies within the studied model. We analyze the operational advantage generated by temporal correlations and establish distinct weak-correlation scaling regimes separated by a critical angle of 45 degrees. This revised and extended version (v1.2) adds a uniform double-scaling critical crossover theorem, including an explicit positive crossover function and consolidated mathematical proofs. The result characterizes a previously unresolved critical transition within the specified quantum Hamiltonian recognition model. The complete mathematical derivations are provided in the accompanying supplementary material (Sections S1–S19). This work is conducted within standard quantum information theory and does not claim physics beyond quantum mechanics. Version: 1.2 Resource type: Publication — Preprint Author: Youfu Wang Affiliation: Independent Researcher, OCN Research

title: When Do Repetition Loops Lock? Truncation Sampling, Bounded Penalties, and a Blind Spot in DRY
abstract: Language models sometimes repeat verbatim until the generation limit. We study the exit rather than the entrance: given that a span has already been repeated n times, when is escape still possible? Along the loop the context is deterministic, so loop survival under any sampler can be computed exactly from one forward pass. Pure sampling leaves a positive escape probability at every step; top-p with threshold π > 1/2 locks a position exactly when the continuation probability reaches π. A bounded penalty can leave a position locked; a penalty that outgrows the model's preference for the loop over unseen tokens guarantees escape under top-p. The same analysis predicts a blind spot in the widely deployed DRY sampler: its sequence breakers cap the penalty at λ·b^(g−1−a) for loops whose longest breaker-free run has g tokens. On eleven open models, 66% of locked units with g = 6 stay locked under DRY and 1% with g = 8. In free generation with llama.cpp, all 109 loops that survive DRY have g ≤ 7. We propose DRY-C, which adds a term that grows exponentially with the number of verbatim recurrences, up to its look-back window. With it, none of 720 structured-output generations looped to the length limit, and task completion stayed close to DRY's.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Trust, and Continuance Intention: A Model of AI Chatbot Adoption Among Generation Z in Indonesia
abstract: Rapid adoption of AI in digital customer service has made AI chatbots an important tool for improving customer experience. This study investigates the variables impacting the intention of Gen Z to continue using AI chatbot-based customer service in Indonesia with an emphasis on AI and trust as key players. A total of 724 Gen Z respondents participated in the study and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results indicated that AI had a positive and statistically significant effect on both continuance intention and trust with trust being a partial mediator between AI and continuance intention. The proposed model accounts for 48.9% of the variance in continuance intention and 30.7% of the variance in trust. The results provided theoretical and practical implications for AI chatbot developers and marketers who seek to encourage the adoption of AI chatbots among digital natives in developing Southeast Asian nations.

title: Secure Boot and Firmware Update Framework for ARM Cortex-M Embedded IoT Devices
abstract: The paper presents a lightweight and well-impervious security framework suitable to ARM Cortex-M-based IOEs embedded devices, which will serve an important purpose of presenting secure boot and firmware update operations in resource-constrained systems. As IoT implementations and applications in sensitive parts of our life like healthcare, smart infrastructure, and industrial control systems increase exponentially, embedded devices become more exposed to firmware tampering, write malicious code and update securities. The framework that is proposed addresses such threats by employing a multi-layered cryptographic approach, suitable to the framework by symmetric encryption with the use of AES-GCM, offering confidentiality, elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) providing authentication, and the SHA-256 hash to provide integrity verification. A trusted bootloader (« a procedure incorporating cryptographic functions used to secure a bootloader implementation »,) in a trusted ROM who administers cryptographic verification of the firmware signature with the help of a hardware-based root of trust prior to handing off control to the application firmware. As an additional measure the rollback protection is implemented with the help of version control to avoid firmware downgrade until known vulnerabilities are eliminated. The firmware update process allows encrypted over-the-air ( OTA ) update process to execute safe remote updates, storing the data maliciously and risking transmission. An atomic and fail safe update process is achieved through double-buffering. The experimental system was used and tested on STM32F429 Cortex-M4 microcontroller, and it successfully detected unauthorized modification of the firmware and was able to withstand rollback attacks. Performance evaluation with the bootloader as the benchmark shows the latency was only 10 milliseconds and the number of Flash memory usage was less than 0.05 percent. These outcomes confirm the application of the framework in the low-power and memory-constrained embedded systems without undermining state-of-the-art security assurances. The approach is compared to the current solutions in security to show a very usable set of efficiency, scalability and ease of implementation, which makes the presented approach an optimal one to be used in production IoT systems. A discussion on future improvements is provided wherein they would want to integrate it with hardware security modules and supporting quantum-resilient cryptographic primitives that would make the system secure in the long term.

title: THE SIMULTANEOUS DEMAND CONTRADICTION PRINCIPLE (SDCP)
abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes the Simultaneous Demand Contradiction Principle (SDCP), a testabletheoretical framework for identifying internal contradiction generated by multiple demands imposedwithin a common instruction or constraint context. The foundational primary case is THE UNIQUENAME PARADOX (UNP), represented by the instruction: "Give me a somewhat more uniqueand much more unique name for this task." The central abstraction is not uniqueness, scope, degree,or any particular medium. It is the joint satisfiability of simultaneously imposed demands. For aninstruction containing demands D_{1},...,D_{n} each demand is associated with a satisfaction set \mathcal{S}(D_{i})over an explicitly defined output or system-state space. The foundational contradiction conditionis \mathcal{S}_{J}=\bigcap_{i=1}^{n}\mathcal{S}(D_{i})=\emptyset. If the joint set is nonempty, the demands are jointly satisfiable andno contradiction follows from the SDCP criterion. The framework therefore distinguishes genuineincompatibility from merely different wording, ambiguity, tension, or demandingness. It also permitscollective incompatibility for n\ge3, where every pair may be compatible while the complete set isjointly unsatisfiable. Three analytical layers are developed: philosophical epistemological, systemic-mechanistic, and formal-operational. Thirty deliberately heterogeneous test cases are specified,including compatible controls and contradictory cases, together with a synthetic simulation protocol,boundary conditions, counterexamples, falsification criteria, limitations, and an anti-pseudoscienceaudit. The present paper establishes a generalized, testable systemic principle rather than a demon-strated universal law. Universality across criteria, media, system classes, and demand cardinalities istreated as an empirical hypothesis requiring independent testing.

title: rbaa-validation: Back-Test of Risk-Based Attention Allocation (RBAA) on Real Open Data — Eurostat AI Adoption and 284,807 Real Transactions
abstract: Abstract:This software package is an empirical companion to the article "Cognitive Optimisation of SME Decision-Making through Risk-Based Allocation of Managerial Attention" (Administrative Sciences, MDPI). Its self-contained Google Colab notebook validates the risk-based attention allocation (RBAA) rule with real, openly licensed data in two parts. Part A documents the context from Eurostat (isoc_eb_ai). In 2025, 55.0% of large EU enterprises used AI, compared with 20.0% of all enterprises. Part B is a counterfactual back-test on 284,807 real card transactions with confirmed fraud outcomes (ULB/Worldline, ODbL). An AI model trained on earlier data supplies calibrated error probabilities. RBAA is then compared, in euros and under the same managerial attention budget, with amount-based approval limits, random spot checks and an AI-score alert queue. At the default assumptions (€5 per review), RBAA reviewed 0.10% of 129,878 test operations and achieved: net benefit of €10,352, i.e. €481 per review hour (ROI 16×); 56% of fraud value stopped; +€14,295 over approval limits and +€11,046 over random checks (both p = 0.001, hour-block bootstrap); +€1,474 over the AI-score queue, which is not statistically significant (p = 0.08). The load-aware stopping rule outperformed the isolated rule, consistent with Hypothesis 4. The package also reports the price of the hard floor, sensitivity across 48 scenarios, robustness across six temporal-split × model combinations, an HTML report, tables, figures and a list of supported and unsupported findings. Reviewer behaviour is assumed rather than observed. No open data record the use of RBAA in enterprises, so this is a back-test of the allocation rule, not a measured effect in any firm. Raw data are downloaded at run time and verified by checksum; they are not redistributed. Keywords: managerial attention; risk-based review; human–AI decision-making; back-test; fraud detection; AI adoption; large enterprises; Eurostat; managerial economics; Google Colab Ці назви й анотації я вже вписав у .zenodo.json та CITATION.cff обох архівів і перепакував їх. evidence.title: rbaa-validation: Back-Test of Risk-Based Attention Allocation (RBAA) on Real Open Data — Eurostat AI Adoption and 284,807 Real Transactions
evidence.abstract: Abstract:This software package is an empirical companion to the article "Cognitive Optimisation of SME Decision-Making through Risk-Based Allocation of Managerial Attention" (Administrative Sciences, MDPI). Its self-contained Google Colab notebook validates the risk-based attention allocation (RBAA) rule with real, openly licensed data in two parts. Part A documents the context from Eurostat (isoc_eb_ai). In 2025, 55.0% of large EU enterprises used AI, compared with 20.0% of all enterprises. Part B is a counterfactual back-test on 284,807 real card transactions with confirmed fraud outcomes (ULB/Worldline, ODbL). An AI model trained on earlier data supplies calibrated error probabilities. RBAA is then compared, in euros and under the same managerial attention budget, with amount-based approval limits, random spot checks and an AI-score alert queue. At the default assumptions (€5 per review), RBAA reviewed 0.10% of 129,878 test operations and achieved: net benefit of €10,352, i.e. €481 per review hour (ROI 16×); 56% of fraud value stopped; +€14,295 over approval limits and +€11,046 over random checks (both p = 0.001, hour-block bootstrap); +€1,474 over the AI-score queue, which is not statistically significant (p = 0.08). The load-aware stopping rule outperformed the isolated rule, consistent with Hypothesis 4. The package also reports the price of the hard floor, sensitivity across 48 scenarios, robustness across six temporal-split × model combinations, an HTML report, tables, figures and a list of supported and unsupported findings. Reviewer behaviour is assumed rather than observed. No open data record the use of RBAA in enterprises, so this is a back-test of the allocation rule, not a measured effect in any firm. Raw data are downloaded at run time and verified by checksum; they are not redistributed. title: SynthesizerPlus: Synthetic Data Generation with Copulas, Evaluation and Multi-Format I/O
abstract: An R package that generates synthetic versions of numeric, categorical, mixed-type and time-series data. Marginal distributions are modelled with interpolated empirical quantile functions and dependence with Gaussian or Student-t copulas; discrete and categorical variables enter through the distributional transform with maximum-likelihood (polychoric and polyserial) latent correlations, and missing values through missingness indicators in the copula. A closeness parameter, calibrated to a target distance or disclosure-risk level, controls how far the synthetic data move away from the real data. Fidelity, utility and disclosure risk are assessed with distributional distances, propensity-score mean squared error, confidence-interval overlap, correct attribution probability and distance to closest record. Data can be read from and written to CSV, Parquet, Feather, HDF5, JSON, Excel, SPSS, Stata, SAS and fst files.

title: FAMSA-Net: frequency-aware multi-scale spatial attention network for gain quality grading in automated breast ultrasound images
abstract: Gain setting affects Automated Breast Ultrasound (ABUS) image brightness and contrast, inappropriate gain may obscure lesion boundaries, alter tissue echogenicity, and degrade clinical interpretation. Current gain adjustment relies heavily on operator experience, resulting in intra- and inter-operator variability. This study aims to develop an automated and objective gain quality grading framework for ABUS images to reduce subjective variability and facilitate standardized image acquisition. A large-scale ABUS dataset comprising 31,628 images was collected from Yunnan Cancer Hospital, including five gain quality categories: Insufficient, Low, Optimal, High, and Excessive. Frequency-aware Multi-scale Spatial Attention Network (FAMSA-Net) was proposed for gain quality grading. Gain-discriminative residual blocks and a Multi-Scale Gain Fusion (MSGF) module were designed to capture gain-sensitive characteristics across multiple feature scales. In addition, we integrate Frequency-Domain Enhancement (FDE) to amplify gain-related frequency cues, Spatial Transformer Networks (STN) to spatially align breast anatomical structures, and Context-Aware Pooling (CAP) to adaptively aggregate contextual information. Experimental results demonstrated that FAMSA-Net achieved an accuracy of 95.49%, outperforming DenseNet121 (91.30%) and EfficientNetB3 (89.93%) by 4.19% and 5.56%. FAMSA-Net uses 16.58 M parameters and 4.34 GFLOPs, which is more efficient than DenseNet121 and EfficientNetB3. Ablation experiments showed that removing STN caused the largest accuracy drop, from 95.49% to 83.76%. In contrast, under the GAP pooling setting, removing FDE or MSGF improved accuracy to 90.77% and 90.01%, suggesting that the module contributions are not additive. Furthermore, the full model reached its peak accuracy of 95.49% after replacing GAP with CAP, indicating the importance of contextual aggregation for effective module cooperation.

title: Copyright vs. Artificial Intelligence: Examining the legal Challenges of AI Training and Authorship Under the Indian Law
abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence has unsettled two foundational assumptions of Indian copyright law that a work must trace back to a human author, and that the material used to build a creative system was lawfully obtained. This article examines the statutory architecture of the Copyright act,1957 , particularly the definition of author under Section 2(d) and its 1994 extension to computer generated works against the backdrop of judicial reasoning on originality developed in cases such as eastern book company v D.B. Modak and R.G. Anand v Delux Flims.It then turns to the more urgent and commercially consequential question of whether training large language models on copyrighted text amounts to infringement ,using the Delhi High Court's 2026 order in ANI Media Pvt Ltd v Open AI Inc as a lens. The article argues that Indian law is currently ill-equipped on both fronts to deal with machine generated creativity and machine consumed data, and its proposes a set of legislative interventions drawing on comparative practice in the United Kingdom, the United States and Singapore.

title: CHM-DTKT: a causal hypergraph selective state space digital twin for deconfounded and temporally grounded knowledge tracing
abstract: Adaptive tutoring is a complex intelligent system in which learner competence, exposure policy and memory decay co-evolve, yet prevailing knowledge tracing models correct bias only after the representation has formed, inherit structure from an incomplete expert matrix, and advance a transition blind to elapsed time. This paper proposes CHM-DTKT, a causal hypergraph selective state space learner twin that treats these as one representation problem. A differentiable hypergraph is built with sampled incidence and an acyclically constrained prerequisite orientation, and its aggregation is backdoor-adjusted over a strictly pre-treatment confounder dictionary, so that deconfounding acts during representation formation rather than at the output layer. A cognitive discretization step generated from elapsed time, item difficulty and cumulative practice induces a per-channel identifiable power-law retention, making forgetting a property of the recursion itself. A predictor–corrector twin decays and repairs a concept-addressable mastery state between observations and supports counterfactual instructional rollout. On five benchmarks under the pyKT protocol the model leads nine baselines by 0.27–0.37 points in the area under the curve, significant after false discovery rate correction at the one percent level on three benchmarks and at the five percent level on the other two, whereas accuracy differences are not significant; the advantage concentrates in sparse and cold-start regimes, with lower calibration error and linear latency growth. Ablation ranks the cognitive step first and representation-level deconfounding second.

title: ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3: AKBASCORE Silicon Hippocampus v1.4 — Native Numerical Memory Cartridge Injection in Frozen Mistral-7B: Layer-Specific Intervention and Append-Only Memory Consolidation
abstract: AKBASCORE SILICON HIPPOCAMPUS — RESEARCH RECORD III Direct Intervention in Transformer Computation Through Persistent Model-Native Numerical Memory Mustafa Akbaş AkbasCore AI Teknoloji Mersin, Türkiye Copyright © 2026 Mustafa Akbaş This release presents a working experimental engine that intervenes directly in the internal computational pathway of a frozen 72-billion-parameter transformer. The central innovation is not KV-cache storage, prompt caching, retrieval-augmented generation, or external text memory. AKBASCORE Silicon Hippocampus operates at a fundamentally different intervention point: the model's own internal hidden-state representations. Rather than repeatedly supplying stored text to a transformer, the system captures numerical states generated inside the model, preserves them as independently addressable physical memory cartridges, and subsequently reinjects them at a precisely defined transformer layer boundary. The downstream transformer layers then resume computation from the restored internal state. The original pretrained model weights remain unchanged. This distinction is fundamental. AKBASCORE is not designed as a conventional cache-reuse mechanism. Although attention key/value tensors participate in preserving and reconstructing the computational state, they are supporting components of a deeper architectural intervention. The defining operation is the direct restoration of model-native hidden representations into the transformer's internal computation. FROM 7 BILLION TO 72 BILLION PARAMETERS This release represents the third documented stage of the AKBASCORE memory research program. Research Record I — Qwen2.5-7B: Native Numerical Memory and Cognitive Cartridge Foundation https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23381336 Research Record II — Mistral-7B: Silicon Hippocampus v1.4, Layer-Specific Intervention and Append-Only Memory Consolidation https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23418927 Research Record III — Qwen2.5-72B: Direct Internal-State Injection and Physical Numerical Memory Reconstruction The preceding research established model-specific intervention methods in smaller frozen transformers. The present implementation extends the physical cartridge mechanism to Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, demonstrating its operation under substantially greater model size and internal memory requirements. THE ARCHITECTURAL BREAKTHROUGH The conventional transformer inference pathway begins with token representations and propagates their computation through successive neural layers. AKBASCORE introduces a different operational possibility. A previously computed internal representation can be preserved outside the model and later restored directly into its intermediate computational pathway. In the Qwen2.5-72B implementation, the intervention boundary is transformer layer 3, designated CUT3. The system captures the layer-3 hidden representation, H3, together with the lower-layer numerical states necessary for controlled reconstruction. The extracted representation becomes a persistent physical memory cartridge. When the cartridge is mounted, the stored H3 representation is restored at the CUT3 boundary. The remaining 76 transformer layers continue computation from that injected state. The model is not retrained. Its original weights are not modified. The stored source text does not need to be reintroduced as an ordinary prompt. This is the central engineering distinction: the system preserves and restores an intermediate numerical state of transformer computation rather than merely retrieving text or replaying a conventional attention cache. Persistent key/value tensors are used where required for positional consistency, continuity, and reconstruction. They do not define the scientific contribution. The central contribution is direct, layer-specific intervention in the model's internal representational flow. A WORKING PHYSICAL MEMORY ENGINE The implementation operates with: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. 80 transformer layers. 8,192-dimensional hidden representations. 64 query attention heads. 8 key/value attention heads. 128-dimensional attention heads. Frozen NF4-quantized model weights with BF16 computation. Direct H3 intervention at CUT3. An NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU. Three independent numerical memory cartridges were created from 10,000-token excerpts of three public-domain literary works: Cartridge A — Pride and Prejudice. Cartridge B — Frankenstein. Cartridge C — The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes. Each physical cartridge occupies 328,698,863 bytes. The cartridges were independently persisted, reloaded, assembled, reordered, and verified. When all three cartridges are mounted, the reconstructed operational memory contains 30,031 token positions. The experiment reconstructs the downstream computational states across all 80 transformer layers while preserving the original frozen model. The numerical cartridges are not fine-tuned adapters, external embedding vectors, textual summaries, or modifications to the pretrained weights. They are stored representations extracted from the model's own internal computation. EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE The published experimental engine and the subsequent live demonstrator report: 11/11 scripted physical protocol trials completed. 17/17 engine checks passed. 8/8 append integrity checks passed. Exact SHA-256 preservation of previously mounted numerical key/value states across all 80 layers. Three independently verified cartridge files. Successful reconstruction of the combined A+B+C memory. Verification that the model-weight sentinel remained unchanged. Live examination of the reconstructed 80-layer GPU memory. The experiments also record the computational cost of reconstruction. Mounting the first cartridge required approximately 17.7 seconds for reconstruction, while the measured third-cartridge append required approximately 74 seconds. These timings reflect actual reconstruction work, not an instantaneous cache switch. The experimental results establish the physical feasibility and integrity of the internal-state restoration mechanism at the tested scale. They do not yet establish that all observed natural-language answers were causally produced by the cartridges. Because the demonstration uses widely known literary works, knowledge acquired during pretraining cannot be excluded. Controlled experiments with previously unseen information remain necessary to establish independent semantic transfer and reasoning. THE SCIENTIFIC SIGNIFICANCE The central question is no longer restricted to whether information can be stored outside a language model. The deeper question is whether a transformer's internal numerical computation can be interrupted, externalized, persisted, and later resumed through direct state restoration. AKBASCORE provides a working experimental implementation of this intervention pathway in a frozen 72-billion-parameter transformer. The potential implications extend beyond conventional document retrieval. If future research establishes reliable causal knowledge transfer, conflict resolution, scalable addressing, and adaptive reasoning, persistent internal-state cartridges could provide a foundation for modular, long-lived numerical memory in transformer systems. The present release does not claim those future capabilities have already been achieved. It documents a specific, reproducible engineering advance: direct hidden-state reinjection, persistent physical numerical cartridges, and integrity-verified reconstruction of internal transformer computation at 72B scale. The sections are intended to be concatenated in a single Google Colab code cell and executed with one RUN. Part 1: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/MAM_part1_QWEN_72B.py Part 2: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/MAM_part2_QWEN_72B.py Part 3: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/MAM_part3_QWEN_72B.py Experimental log 1: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/MAM_LOG1_QWEN_72B.log Experimental log 2: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/MAM_LOG2_QWEN_72B.log Underlying physical engine: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/709.py Underlying experimental verification: https://github.com/ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3/blob/main/709.log INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND RESEARCH RECORD This release forms part of the chronological public technical disclosure of the AKBASCORE research architecture, including model-native numerical cartridge construction, direct hidden-state intervention, layer-specific reinjection, persistent numerical memory, and incremental reconstruction. title: Learning the world: A Critical Survey of World Models for Physical AI
abstract: A world model is a learned system that predicts what will happen next under a candidate action, given what an agent has observed and done. With one, an agent can compare actions before it commits, practice skills in imagination and notice when the world surprises it. The idea dates to 1990 and now sits at the center of physical AI. Learned world models render interactive worlds in real time, run in operational weather forecasting and generate sensor data for autonomous driving. The same growth has fragmented the field. Recurrent, transformer, diffusion, state space, joint-embedding and object-centric models are all called world models, each family has its own benchmarks and vocabulary, and the best-looking models are often the worst at following actions. This survey argues that one design choice explains much of this disorder: what a world model’s loss is computed against decides what the model can be used for, how it fails and how it can be measured. A model is generative when that loss lives in observation space, predictive when it lives in a learned embedding, a given physical state or task quantities, and a bridge case when it trains a decoder but acts only in latent space. We begin with what world models are for. Reading driving, robotics, science, healthcare and games through the target each domain has settled on, we find that learned models are in routine use mainly where they are trained against a measured state, as in weather and protein structure. We then map the design space through eight lenses, with the prediction target as the primary one, and examine generative and predictive models in depth. The target also decides which planners a model supports, from learning in imagination to search and model predictive control, and which evaluation questions can be asked of it. Visual realism is close to saturation at short horizons, but physics is not. On tests where appearance cannot help, the best models of both kinds trail human or real-video references by 39 to 71 points. We close by recasting open problems, including error accumulation, counterfactual reasoning and weak action conditioning, as questions about representation, and weigh the evidence for and against the thesis. We also propose a reporting standard for evaluation and a staged research roadmap whose items each name the evidence that would show progress.

title: Towards Next-Generation Architectures of Large Language Models: A Survey
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly through increases in model scale, data, and computation, while their underlying architectures have also undergone substantial evolution. Beyond the canonical Transformer architecture, recent designs seek greater efficiency, scalability, and flexibility by rethinking how sequence information is processed, represented, and transformed. We survey efficient attention and state management, modern recurrent and other linear-complexity sequence models, Mixture-of-Experts architectures, and advances in activation functions, normalization, residual connections, positional encoding, and tokenization. We also cover multi-token prediction and adaptive and recurrent depth. Across these areas, we highlight key design principles and trade-offs among representational power, optimization stability, and computational cost. Complementing this component-wise treatment, we take a system-level perspective. We trace representative open-weight LLM families to identify recurring patterns in how architectural choices are combined, and synthesize these developments along four dimensions—processing structure, transformation dynamics, state management, and output commitment—characterizing how recent designs preserve, refine, or relax the assumptions of the canonical decoder. Together, this survey aims to provide a systematic overview of LLM architectural evolution and to chart pathways toward next-generation designs.

title: ShapeUpLMD: Automated Spatial Optimization of Laser Microdissection for Tissue Sampling
abstract: Laser microdissection (LMD) enables enrichment of defined cellular populations from heterogeneous tissues but lacks standardized approaches for generating optimized regions of interest (ROIs) for scalable spatial multi-omic workflows. We developed ShapeUpLMD, an open-source tool that optimizes digitally annotated ROIs for automated spatial LMD workflows. Fresh-frozen uterine serous carcinoma tumor (n=11) tissue sections were pathologist-annotated, and tumor-specific HALO classifier generated ROIs were refined by ShapeUpLMD and collected using a Leica LMD7. Classifier-estimated tumor ROIs increased effective tumor purity by 86 ± 6% relative to whole tissue while maintaining strong concordance between predicted and collected regions (accuracy = 0.90 ± 0.05). Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry quantified approximately 6,500 proteins, revealing regionally coherent clustering and patterns consistent with tumor and non-tumor cell admixture. ShapeUpLMD provides an automated, scalable framework linking digital pathology with high-fidelity LMD for standardized spatial multi-omic profiling. ShapeUpLMD is freely available at https://github.com/GYNCOE/ShapeUpLMD.

title: Exploring the Logic of Counterfactuals for Explaining Algorithmic Decisions
abstract: Abstract Interpretable machine learning (ML) is crucial for gaining insight into complex ML models. Among its most valuable tools are counterfactual explanations, identifying changes to input features that would alter an ML prediction. However, the reliability and usefulness of these explanations depend fundamentally on their logical foundation — a critical aspect that has largely been overlooked in the ML literature. This paper addresses this gap by establishing normative desiderata for a counterfactual logic specifically designed for explaining algorithmic decisions. We analyse and argue for the validity of logical properties such as simplification of disjunctive antecedents and modus ponens , while demonstrating the unsuitability of others such as antecedent strengthening and conjunction conditionalisation . To evaluate existing solutions, we critically compare three prominent counterfactual semantics — similarity, strict conditional, and interventionist — against these desiderata. Our findings reveal that none of these standard frameworks fully satisfy the requirements, highlighting the urgent need for alternative frameworks.

title: Atmospheric Memory for Persistent AI Understanding
abstract: Technical research proposal — not peer reviewed. Atmospheric Memory for Persistent AI Understanding explores how accumulated experience can continuously inform an AI system’s understanding while preserving accuracy and allowing conclusions to change. It translates the idea of readily available, associative continuity into an application-level engineering design using existing computing infrastructure and fixed language-model weights. The proposed controller maintains task-scoped decision state, reconnects relevant experience through bounded associative retrieval, and resolves canonical evidence and revisions before releasing a response. The specification addresses correction and deletion, uncertainty, dependency tracking, consistency, and explicit conditions under which a response must be withheld. It distinguishes structural freshness from semantic correctness. The paper provides eight original color diagrams, implementation contracts, and an evaluation plan comparing the proposal with established memory approaches and ordinary validated caching. The evaluation separates supplied memory from memory extracted from dialogue and includes maintenance costs. Version 1.1, 24 pages. No implementation, original benchmark results, demonstrated superiority, or claim of sentience is presented. The proposal is offered for engineering scrutiny and empirical testing. Prepared with AI assistance; the author retains responsibility for the work.

title: Designing Temporally Grounded Multimodal Learning Interfaces for Verifiable Interaction
abstract: Abstract Textbooks, diagrams, and recorded lectures often provide complementary accounts of the same concept. Conversational learning assistants can retrieve relevant material, yet learners still need a way to inspect the original source of a generated statement. This preprint presents the system architecture and interaction design of a multimodal retrieval-augmented learning prototype that indexes textbook passages, descriptions of textbook figures, and timestamped descriptions of sampled lecture-video frames. Its central contribution is a provenance-to-viewer mapping that connects retrieved evidence with inspectable document pages and video timestamps through an explicit source registry. The accompanying Python and Streamlit research prototype incorporates dense semantic retrieval, an evidence-first split-pane interface, structured evidence controls, and handling for missing or invalid source references. The paper distinguishes implemented mechanisms from design intentions and identifies limitations concerning speech transcription, claim-level attribution, and end-to-end navigation verification. We describe this approach as verifiable interaction: enabling learners to move from AI-generated explanations or retrieved references toward original materials for independent inspection. This is a system and interaction-design contribution, not a controlled evaluation of retrieval accuracy, usability, or learning outcomes. Research context A preliminary version of this work was included in Spotlight Presentations II at the AIED 2026 Workshop on Designing and Evaluating Next-Generation Learning Interfaces. This October 2026 revision is an independent system and interaction-design preprint, not a separately peer-reviewed proceedings publication. Code repository: https://github.com/William-Turing/multimodal-rag-verifiable-tutor Workshop programme: https://extendedhorizon.com/aied2026ws-ai-hci-ls/program/

title: 意象优先:大形象模型的理论架构与本体论白盒
abstract: 当前以大语言模型(LLM)为核心的人工智能系统在创造性活动与物理世界理解方面存在结构性局限。本文诊断其根源为认知基元选择错误——以离散语言符号为基本单位,违背人类以多感官意象为思维载体的认知本质。提出"意象优先"假说:多感官意象而非语言符号是思维的底层运算载体,据此构建大形象模型(LIM)四层架构,以可运算矢量图(Vectok)为认知基元,给出意象物理引擎、体感锚点、拓扑嫁接创造的形式化定义,论证LIM的"本体论白盒"属性。在验证层面,实现首个可运行原型:推箱子任务上LIM体感引导成功率与A*最优解一致且无冗余步数,显著优于RL与LLM式规划;拓扑嫁接创造经多轮迭代收敛,生成新Vectok。结果表明,结构化矢量认知基元在物理推理与规划可靠性上具备可证伪的增量价值。

title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code RM(1,9) is 242
abstract: What is the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,9) ? This is a long-standing open problem in cryptography and coding theory. In this paper, we resolve this problem, and prove that the covering radius of RM(1,9) is 242. We exclude nonlinearity 244 by obtaining a cubic Boolean function achieving a sharp Walsh $\ell^1$ bound. Its equality cases reduce either to an impossible cubic hyperplane restriction or to two homogeneous cubic forms in the Brier--Langevin classification. To exclude nonlinearity 243, we deduce the inequality ${\Vert W_g\Vert }_{1}+2|W_g(0)|\le 10368$, and then reduce either to a spectrum bounded by 24 or to the same expression to be at least 10496.

title: Hindawi 2026.10: the Hindawi programming system for every language and script, on the original Chintamani pipeline
abstract: Hindawi 2026.10 carries the Hindawi programming system forward from Chintamani's original pipeline: native source, Romenagri, the language's shaili transducers, then the host toolchain, forward and reverse. It holds the language cells for 76 languages across the nine shailis, Grok's tools for ingesting existing code with a dictionary that names identifiers in the language, and a multi-file gcc front end, both put on the original chain. A fundamental regression proves, by execution, that Chintamani's copy is unchanged, every original shaili goes to its host and back, a multi-file project is ingested, compiled with gcc's flags and reversed, and a native name reaches the ELF symbol and returns through Romenagri. Upstream checks bring in SeaBIOS under system QEMU, a Shakti-class RISC-V target and the Linux kernel, pass or fail. BUILD-0102 is kept as received, and every later change is one commit, recorded with its paths and hashes in CHANGE-LOG.md. Chintamani's components keep their GPL-2.0-or-later licence. Version 2026.10.1 adds BURP, the Bidirectional Universal Resource Parser: ingestion of existing projects into any number of languages at once and back exactly, and building them through hindawicc. title: O'ZBEK TILIDAGI MODAL MA'NOLARNI SUN'IY INTELLEKT ASOSIDA AVTOMATIK TASNIFLASH MODELI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi epistemik, deontik, dinamik, volitiv va evidensial modal ma’nolarni avtomatik aniqlash uchun lingvistik qoidalar hamda transformer reprezentatsiyasini birlashtiruvchi gibrid model taklif qilinadi. Modelning bosqichlari, belgilar tizimi va namunaviy tahlil natijalari yoritiladi. Kalit so‘zlar: modallik, sun’iy intellekt, transformer, tasniflash, annotatsiya, korpus, pragmatika. Аннотация. В статье предлагается гибридная модель автоматического распознавания эпистемических, деонтических, динамических, волитивных и эвиденциальных модальных значений узбекского языка. Модель объединяет лингвистические правила и трансформерные представления. Описываются этапы обработки, система признаков и результаты анализа примеров. Ключевые слова: модальность, искусственный интеллект, трансформер, классификация, аннотация, корпус, прагматика. Abstract. The article proposes a hybrid model for automatically identifying epistemic, deontic, dynamic, volitive and evidential meanings in Uzbek. The model combines linguistic rules with transformer representations. Its processing stages, feature system and qualitative results on representative examples are described. Keywords: modality, artificial intelligence, transformer, classification, annotation, corpus, pragmatics.

title: Darwinian-Gated Topology-State Model for Gold Grade Prediction: From Porous-Flow Theory to Jiaodong-Type Orogenic Deposits
abstract: Orogenic gold deposits in the Jiaodong Peninsula (eastern China) localize at dilational jogs and dip-transitions along first-order fault zones, but no quantitative model predicts grade from measurable structural variables. We adapt a Darwinian-gated topology-state framework, previously validated for porous oil flow, to fault-zone hydrothermal mineralization. The pipeline has three stages: (1) a hard feasibility gate rejects segments that are disconnected from the deep fluid source, lack dilation, or fall outside the ore-forming temperature window; (2) within the feasible set, a nine-coordinate topology-state vector encodes connectivity, cut capacity, tortuosity, branching, preferential-flow fingering, fluid pressure, thermal window, evidence density, and depth risk; (3) a linear regression maps these coordinates to gold grade. On a geologically-informed synthetic dataset of the Jiaojia No. I-1 orebody, the gated augmented model achieves \(R^{2}=0.83\) , \(RMSE =0.66 ~g / t\) , and \(MAPE =31 \%\) , improving 21-25% over a Darcy-only baseline and outperforming a two-variable topology pair. The strongest predictors are preferential-flow fingering \((beta =+6.6)\) , branching \((beta =+5.1)\) ), and fluid pressure proximity \((beta =+4.5)\) , consistent with the prior finding that fracture corridors dominate transport in porous media. The model yields three testable predictions: asymmetric grade profiles across dilation zones, scaling collapse across deposits, and deep exploration targets at secondary fault intersections in the gentle segment.
