title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: What a Hallucination Benchmark Measures, and What It Does Not A Format-Controlled Audit of Structural Classification
abstract: Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\)). On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check. We report this figure and then show, using a format-controlled negative (N1) on the same 1,800 IDs, that it measures format asymmetry between source and response rather than hallucination detection. The tribunal flags 1,569 of 1,800 verbatim correct answers presented alone (87.2%), and in HaluEval-QA scores the correct answer as _more_ anomalous than the hallucinated response. Three further findings follow from the same audit. (i) A per-module analysis shows the tribunal has no content-sensitive module in its current set: the one module designed to capture semantic divergence (cre_isi) gives the same per-ID score whether the response is byte-identical or completely different. (ii) The 87.97-point advantage of multiplicative combination over weighted averaging reported in v4 is an artifact of threshold calibration; under per-scheme thresholds on format-matched negatives, both schemes converge to F1 \(\approx 0.69\) and the multiplicative scheme is worse by AUROC. (iii) A new differential guard (R3.1, grounding-based with compression abstention and short-response heuristics) corrects 1,133 of the 1,569 format-driven false positives on correct answers alone, raising F1 from 0.687 to 0.833 (\(\Delta\)F1 = \(+ 0.146\)), and generalizes to a financial domain (FinQA, 1,657 samples) with 87.0% detection and zero regressions. The guard does not rely on substring matching and is not a constructional artifact. The paper’s contribution is the audit procedure that produced these retirements. Five of v4/v5’s quantitative claims do not survive it. What does survive — thresholds, the \(\kappa_{R}\) sweep, the forensic audit of v2 metrics, the per-module architecture itself as a diagnostic instrument — is reported with the same standard.

title: Разработка программного модуля для комплексной оценки качества псевдослучайных последовательностей
abstract: В статье представлена разработка программного модуля для комплексной оценки качества генераторов псевдослучайных чисел (PRNG) с использованием расширенного набора статистических тестов и механизмов параллельной обработки данных. Актуальность работы обусловлена растущими требованиями к надежности криптографических систем в условиях цифровой трансформации и увеличения вычислительной мощности потенциальных злоумышленников. Модуль реализует 31 статистический тест, в том числе 15 тестов NIST STS, 12 тестов Diehard, а также 4 специализированные проверки, и поддерживает три генератора разных классов: Вихрь Мерсенна, CryptMT и криптографически безопасную систему RandomNumberGenerator. Ключевой особенностью решения является параллельное выполнение наборов тестов на основе библиотеки параллелизма задачам и механизма генератора ThreadLocal, что обеспечивает 3–5-кратное ускорение обработки данных на 8-ядерных системах по сравнению с последовательным режимом, гарантируя при этом воспроизводимость результатов для детерминированных генераторов. Модульная трёхуровневая архитектура на платформе C#/.NET 7 позволяет расширять список поддерживаемых генераторов и тестов без изменения ядра системы. В ходе экспериментов генератор Вихрь Мерсенна продемонстрировал скорость генерации 148 миллионов чисел в секунду, пройдя при этом 98% тестов, а потребление оперативной памяти модулем не превышало 650 МБ при обработке выборок объемом до 10 ГБ. Практическая значимость данного решения подтверждается его применимостью к верификации криптографических систем, научным исследованиям и образованию.

title: Relations Acting on Relations: A Layered Conjecture Statement with Definitions, Status and Refutation Conditions
abstract: The research programme asks whether, in systems whose parts are relations, a relation can act on the update rule of another relation, and whether such second-order structure is functionally indispensable. This statement fixes one core claim, an existence claim (C1), defines its terms operationally (intervention-based “effective rule”, functional necessity) and proves it in a toy class by a closed-form comparison: with regime-dependent observation noise, the best state-dependent gain has strictly lower steady-state error than any uniform gain (14–27% in state-estimation error, 1–4% in prediction error for the parameters checked). The toy result did not transfer to the delta-rule engine of the testbed: an oracle regime-dependent scalar gain gave no measurable benefit, and an oracle relation-specific gating gave a structure-dependent but sub-percent benefit. Four further questions are explicitly not part of the core claim and are stated with their status: whether such rules emerge from learning (Q2), reflexive organisation (Q3), a conditional functional candidate for consciousness (Q4), and a heuristic question about non-propagating connection (Q5). The statement gives a status table, refutation conditions, the relation to existing work (metaplasticity, neuromodulated plasticity, fast weights, hypernetworks, adaptive networks) and a list of challenges for readers. Not a proof; not peer reviewed. Companion to doi:10.5281/zenodo.23006539, 23192515, 23373288, 23384438 and 23420727. Proposition 1 is reproduced by the attached script prop1_check.py. AI use: derivations, scripts and drafting were produced with substantial assistance from AI systems; the author is responsible for all content.

title: Mathematicians in the Age of AGI: From Prover to Contemplative Freedom
abstract: README Mathematicians in the Age of AGI: From Prover to Contemplative Freedom This preprint is a working-thought record on the role of mathematicians in the AGI era. It argues that AGI’s cognitive ceiling is geometric, not computational: on the Tarski boundary layer, the tangent and cotangent bundles do not commute, so traversal search fails. The mathematician’s position is not inside the manifold but on the boundary—where projection switching, not search, is the only viable operation. The book has five chapters. Chapter 1 establishes cognitive constraints via the cognitive manifold. Chapter 2 reframes mathematics as mathematical engineering: proofs are cheap, frameworks are not; the mathematician’s output is an interface specification, not a theorem. Chapter 3 identifies three capacities—cross-branch fusion, intuition and inspiration, space and geometry. Chapter 4 defines observing freedom (观自在) as breaking the knowledge obstacle (知见障): seeing the projection itself. Chapter 5 proposes Tian Dao (天道)—respecting the laws of development rather than forcing intervention. The appendices compare these constraints with Baire category theorem and uniform boundedness principle as parallel references. Keywords: AGI; mathematical proof; cognitive manifold; Tarski boundary layer; framework design; observing freedom; Tian Dao; open-source tradition; preprint. License: CC BY 4.0. Knowledge belongs to all humanity.

title: A Cryptographic Abstraction Layer for Integrating NIST Lightweight Cryptography into TLS 1.3
abstract: In the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) domain, security solutions must remain energy-efficient and reliable under strict latency and real-time requirements, especially for resource-constrained devices.Lightweight Cryptography (LWC) has emerged as a feasible solution to these challenges, offering new cryptographic algorithms developed for IIoT environments.The practical integration of LWC into standardized security protocols remains largely unexplored.In this work, we propose a new Transport Layer Security (TLS) cipher-suites integration that incorporates lightweight cryptographic algorithms, recommended by National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), through a Cryptographic Abstraction Layer (CAL).Measurements on IIoT devices show that the abstraction comes at modest effort: the dispatch cost of CAL peaks at 13.73% for the smallest records and falls to between zero and 9.52% once payloads pass 128 bytes, with most suites under 4%.In return, the layer separates TLS record processing from the cryptographic implementation, conceals cipher internals from the layers above, provides runtime cipher agility, and a fixed memory footprint across the registered suites.The layer drives different ciphers spanning block, sponge, duplex, and stream constructions through one calling convention, confirming that no single internal structure is assumed.

title: Adaptive Privacy-Preserving Big Data Analytics: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Deterministic Guardrail Framework
authors: Abhinav Kumar Mishra Abhinav Kumar Mishra
abstract: The exponential expansion of consumer financial services has led to massive volumes of structured transaction and account data being migrated to public cloud data lakes for high-throughput distributed analytics. However, financial datasets intrinsically contain sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) subject to stringent regulatory frameworks including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Indian Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act of 2023. Conventional privacy solutions exhibit a debilitating trilemma: cryptographic methods such as Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) impose prohibitive computational latency; static dictionary-based anonymization collapses under schema drift and lexical variations; and unconstrained machine learning classifiers suffer from train/serve distribution shifts where subtle format discrepancies precipitate catastrophic privacy leaks. In this paper, we propose a scalable, cloud-native privacy preserving big data analytics framework anchored by an Adaptive Dual-Tier Privacy Engine. Our architecture couples an adaptive multi-stage gradient boosted decision tree (XGBoost) classifier— trained on a 25-dimensional structural, keyword, sample-level, and regular expression feature space—with deterministic safety-net guardrails (Force-Protect and Force-Keep). This hybrid design guarantees zero exposure of mission-critical identifiers while completely insulating downstream business analytical features against corruption. Masked datasets are securely persisted to AWS S3 and processed through distributed Apache Spark (PySpark) clusters via the S3A connector across four analytical dimensions: descriptive statistics, bivariate fraud detection with two-factor authentication (2FA) correlation, credit risk profiling, and multi tier customer segmentation. Validated against a high-cardinality 100,000-record banking benchmark across 57 attributes, our system demonstrates 100% mitigation of critical PII leakage, overcomes real-world distribution skew on complex identifier formats, preserves analytical utility with zero loss of statistical fidelity, and maintains sub-minute distributed pipeline throughput. Index Terms—Privacy-Preserving Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing, Apache Spark, XGBoost, Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Hybrid Guardrails, Train/Serve Skew, Financial Data Governance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scientific Development and Future Directions
abstract: This study examines the development and intellectual structure of artificial intelligence (AI)-based financial fraud detection through a bibliometric analysis of 2200 Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed journal articles published between 1992 and 2026. The literature has expanded rapidly, with 89.6% of publications appearing since 2018 and an annual growth rate of 29.4%. Research is concentrated in Computer Science and Engineering, whereas Business and Economics account for 9.2% of classified publications. Credit card and payment fraud constitutes the largest research domain (32.0%), followed by banking, loan, and transaction fraud (14.3%), insurance fraud (12.2%), and accounting and financial statement fraud (9.9%). Neural networks and deep learning, ensemble and boosting methods, and classical supervised classifiers are the dominant methodological families. The field has progressively shifted from traditional data-mining and classical machine-learning approaches toward deep learning, ensemble methods, graph neural networks, and explainable AI. Science mapping shows that the intellectual structure remains strongly centered on payment fraud, while accounting and insurance fraud form more distinct research fronts. title: DeepSwarm-DBSCAN: Deep Learning and Swarm Intelligence for Automated Density-Based Clustering
abstract: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise is widely used for unsupervised clustering due to its ability to identify arbitrarily shaped clusters and handle noise. However, its effectiveness strongly depends on appropriate hyperparameter selection, which becomes challenging and computationally expensive for high-dimensional data. This study aims to address this limitation by proposing an automated and scalable optimization framework. The proposed DeepSwarm-DBSCAN framework integrates deep neural networks with an enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to automatically determine optimal DBSCAN hyper- parameters. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Autoencoders (AE) learn compact and meaningful feature representations, projecting high-dimensional data into lower-dimensional latent spaces. An adaptive PSO strategy then searches this reduced space to optimize clustering validity metrics efficiently. Experimental evaluations on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that DeepSwarm-DBSCAN outperforms conventional DBSCAN, achieving clustering accuracies of 92%, 91%, and 94%—with a silhouette coefficient of 0.7 on MNIST—indicating strong cluster coherence. Additionally, the proposed approach reduces hyperparameter optimization runtime by approximately 30% compared to traditional grid search methods. Conclusion: The results confirm that combining deep representation learning with swarm-based optimization provides an effective solution for DBSCAN hyperparameter tuning. DeepSwarm- DBSCAN offers a robust, scalable, and efficient clustering framework suitable for real- world high-dimensional data analysis across diverse application domains. title: Generative deep learning for class imbalance in credit risk modeling: comparative evaluation of synthetic oversampling methods and an elastic oversampling extension
abstract: This paper applies generative deep learning–GAN, VAE, and CVAE–to oversample rare defaults in credit risk modeling, with a posterior binarization procedure introduced to preserve the marginal distribution of dummy features. Using firm- and individual-level default datasets, we compare these methods against SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek, and ADASYN under multiple classifiers. Empirical results show that synthetic oversampling improves recall and disperses feature importance, while generative oversampling tends to sharpen class boundaries, favor precision, and concentrate feature importance. To balance these complementary strengths, we introduce Elastic Oversampling, a parallel hybrid of generative and synthetic approaches with a tunable mixing ratio for the precision–recall trade-off. Elastic Oversampling emphasizes distinctive minority cases through generative methods while constraining unrealistic samples with synthetic methods, offering a flexible and policy-sensitive framework for class-imbalanced credit risk prediction.

title: FFOA: An adaptive swarm optimizer with centered-optimum-bias assessment
abstract: The Fennec Fox Optimization Algorithm (FFOA) is introduced as a fennec-inspired adaptive swarm optimizer for continuous optimization tasks. Its primary proposal is algebraically a current-to-promising differential move; successful-hunt memory and remembered food-cache reuse provide success-history adaptation and archive-assisted variation, while population reduction, local refinement, diversity recovery, and stagnation recovery are generic numerical support operators. The contribution is therefore an explicitly positioned integration and empirical audit, not a wholly new variation primitive. Evaluation uses exact objective-call accounting. Under one deterministic SHA-256 shift per function–dimension cell, FFOA outperforms Chaotic Evolution Optimization (CEO) in 130 of 150 rounded average-FE cells, ties in one, and is slower in 19; this provides no evidence of centered-optimum bias under the tested shifts, but does not establish general translation invariance. In a 14-algorithm analysis, FFOA obtains the best CEO-style cell-level average rank but is not significantly separated from LSHADE. A CEC-2017/2022 campaign covering 82 function–dimension cells, 17 algorithms, and 41,820 seed records ranks LSHADE first overall (3.000) and FFOA second (3.037); a paired cell-rank test finds them practically indistinguishable ( p Holm = 0.527 , r rb = − 0.081 ). A separate five-variant minimal-core ablation over the same 82 cells and 30 seeds per cell ranks the complete model first and shows that six of seven prespecified Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon contrasts are significant. A sensor-network localization case study likewise shows competitive, not dominant, performance.

title: The Navigation of Ignorance: Epistemology, Human Thought, and Experimental Intelligence in the Age of AI
abstract: AI's highest value may not be in producing answers, but in systematically revealing, mapping, and prioritizing the unknown regions of human knowledge while leaving questions of meaning and purpose to human judgment This paper explores a fundamental shift in the role of artificial intelligence: from an answer-generating system to a tool for systematically mapping human ignorance. Rather than treating knowledge as a collection of solutions, it examines how advanced machine intelligence can help identify, navigate, and characterize the boundaries of what remains unknown. The framework is organized around four foundational limits. First, Information Limits examine the historical gaps in recorded thought and the vast domains of human experience lost to history. Second, Experimental Limits are explored through the Tyre Paradox, demonstrating how active learning systems can overcome combinatorial explosions by identifying the most informative experiments rather than attempting exhaustive search. Third, Epistemic Limits investigate how structured failure, illogical pathways, and conceptual reframing can create analytical shortcuts that accelerate discovery. Finally, the Agency Boundary addresses the distinction between machine optimization and human judgment, arguing that while artificial intelligence can expand the landscape of possible answers, humans must ultimately determine which questions are meaningful and worth pursuing. The paper proposes that the primary value of advanced AI is not omniscience but navigational capacity: the ability to reveal the structure of ignorance itself. By exposing connections between successful theories, failed experiments, and unresolved questions, machine intelligence can transform ignorance from an undefined absence into a mappable domain for systematic inquiry. This work forms part of an ongoing research programme investigating the cognitive applications of artificial intelligence within academic environments. Further findings remain under active development and are expected to emerge from a continuing programme of in-house research. Version 3.0 of "The Navigation of Ignorance." This work develops a conceptual framework for understanding artificial intelligence as a system for navigating the boundaries of human knowledge rather than merely generating answers. The paper introduces four domains of limitation: Information Limits, Experimental Limits, Epistemic Limits, and the Agency Boundary. Together these describe how AI may assist scientific inquiry by identifying informative experiments, mapping uncertainty, learning from structured failure, and clarifying the relationship between machine optimization and human judgment. This publication forms part of an ongoing research programme examining the cognitive applications of artificial intelligence in academic inquiry. This publication represents an interim research contribution within an ongoing programme investigating artificial intelligence, epistemology, and scientific discovery. Additional findings remain under active development and have not yet been released. The concepts presented here should be considered part of a broader continuing research agenda.

title: Beyond AI Tutors: A Human-Centred Framework for Goal-Driven Learning Agents in Education
authors: Ghodakhe Keshav, Prof. Y.G.Suryawanshi, Dr. H.B.Jadhav
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing education by offering new ways to explain concepts, support teachers, and personalise student learning. However, many conventional educational chatbots focus on answering individual questions rather than coordinating the complete learning process. Students often need more than an answer: they need a learning plan, suitable practice activities, feedback on mistakes, and guidance about what to study next. Agentic artificial intelligence offers a possible way to coordinate these activities around a defined learning objective. This paper reviews selected research published between 2024 and 2026 on pedagogical AI agents, large language model agents, and agentic systems in education. The reviewed literature highlights opportunities for personalized tutoring, adaptive feedback, assignment support, and teacher assistance. It also identifies concerns involving inaccurate outputs, student dependency, privacy, fairness, accountability, and limited real-world evaluation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a human-centred framework that connects learning-goal identification, task planning, trusted educational resources, instructional support, progress evaluation, and adaptive follow-up. The framework centres student independence, teacher judgement, and responsible data use. It is a conceptual proposal and has not yet been experimentally evaluated. Future research should assess its educational effectiveness, reliability, accessibility, and suitability for different learning environments

title: OmniTFT: an EHR-driven multi-target forecasting model for ICU clinical decision support systems
abstract: Background Accurate multivariate time-series forecasting of vital signs and laboratory results is crucial for electronic health record (EHR)–driven clinical decision support systems in intensive care units (ICUs). However, vital signs are susceptible to noise and exhibit rapid fluctuations, while laboratory results are characterized by missing values and measurement lags, making it challenging to forecast heterogeneous ICU variables within a common framework. Methods We introduce OmniTFT, a Temporal Fusion Transformer-based multi-target forecasting model for ICU EHR time series. OmniTFT combines state-balanced sliding-window sampling with three training regularizers: frequency-aware embedding shrinkage, historical group-entropy regularization, and shock-alignment regularization. A shared backbone with target-specific heads enables multiple forecasting tasks within a common training and inference framework while preserving target-specific temporal resolutions and forecast horizons. OmniTFT was trained on MIMIC-IV ( n = 13,277) and independently validated on two cohorts: the MIMIC-III CareVue cohort ( n = 4,188) and the eICU cohort ( n = 23,238). Component ablation and sampling sensitivity analyses were conducted using a fixed patient partition and ten different training seeds. Results On the MIMIC-IV test set, OmniTFT achieved the lowest MAE for five of eight targets, ranked second for creatinine and respiratory rate, and ranked third for temperature. In a retrospective analysis in eICU, adding the OmniTFT forecast of the subsequent unobserved 24 h to the complete observed record improved discrimination for incident moderate-to-severe acute kidney injury compared with the observed record alone (AUROC 0.763, 95% CI: 0.674–0.852 vs. 0.693, 0.598–0.787, ΔAUROC + 0.070, DeLong p = 0.009), and identified 73.3% vs. 57.8% of subsequent events when 30% of patients were flagged for review. Conclusions OmniTFT provides a shared-backbone framework for forecasting heterogeneous ICU variables while preserving target-specific temporal configurations. Retrospective results in disease-enriched cohorts support broader external validation and suggest its potential as an EHR-integrated forecasting component for clinical decision support.

title: AI-Assisted Early Detection of Breast Cancer Using Histopathological Image Analysis
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers among women worldwide with more than 2.3 million new breast cancer cases diagnosed each year [1], where early detection has a significantly positive effect on patient survival rates. Examination of histopathological features remains the gold standard [2] in the diagnosis of breast cancer, however, clinical histopathological assessment is labor-intensive, time consuming and can potentially have inter-observer variability in the determination of the final clinical diagnosis. The current paper presents an AI-assisted deep learning framework for automatic breast cancer detection using histopathological images. Multiple transfer learning models, including VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, and EfficientNetB5, were evaluated. The proposed framework incorporates data augmentation, mixed precision training, and Binary Focal Loss to improve performance and computational efficiency. Experimental results on a dataset of over 14,000 histopathological images demonstrate that DenseNet121 achieves the best performance, with a test accuracy of 81%, sensitivity of 80.8%, specificity of 76.7%, and ROC-AUC of 0.87. VGG16 also shows stable performance, while ResNet50 suffers from low specificity due to over classification of malignant classes. EfficientNet models exhibit poor generalization and strong class bias. The result highlights the importance of evaluating multiple performance metrics beyond accuracy in medical image classification. The proposed frameworks can assist pathologists by improving diagnostic consistency and reducing workload, making it a practical tool for clinical applications.

title: Sentimentul știrilor - indici ai sentimentului presei românești despre economie
abstract: Archived version of the Sentimentul știrilor project (Romanian news sentiment indices). Sentimentul știrilor measures the tone of Romanian economic news. The system collects about 3.5 million articles from more than 130 Romanian outlets, scores them with lexicon-based methods and locally run language models, and aggregates the scores into public sentiment indices related to macroeconomic indicators and financial markets. The indices, methodology and interactive courses are published at https://sentimentulstirilor.ro (English: https://sentimentulstirilor.ro/en). Part of the doctoral research of Vlad Pineta, PhD candidate in Finance, Bucharest University of Economic Studies.

title: Initiating Conversation: A Proactive Persona Agent with Relationship-Tiered Memory and a Simulated Inner Life
abstract: Most conversational AI systems are strictly reactive, responding only when prompted and remain-ing dormant between user sessions. However, in human relationships, initiating contact serves as afundamental social signal of attention, shared memory, and care. In this paper, we present Liliana, anLLM-based persona agent deployed in a live Discord community that autonomously determines when,to whom, and about what to initiate conversation. Our approach relies on three coupled mechanisms:(1) a simulated inner life, implemented via a scheduler that maintains ongoing agent activities anddaily rituals (e.g., morning reports and nightly diaries) to provide contextual reasons for reachingout; (2) relationship-tiered memory, which tracks persistent per-user state (relationship tier, mood,and a topic ledger) to govern conversational tone, initiation frequency, and social boundaries; and(3) artifact-grounded proactivity, through which the agent creates small digital works (micro-gamesand seeded generative art), shares playable links, solicits user feedback, classifies responses, anddeploys code fixes in a closed loop. We report the system architecture and preliminary telemetryfrom a first-week in-situ deployment in a small private community (N = 4 recurring users). Earlyobservations show a 77% response rate within a 12-hour window (n = 13 messages, largely drivenby interactions with the developer) and an 80% topic-grounding rate among measurable messages(n = 5). We also document practical deployment failure modes, including cross-user mood con-tamination and text-to-speech hallucinations caused by decorative punctuation, alongside the ethicalguardrails required for proactive companion agents.

title: Securing and Governing AI Automation: A Containment-First Approach
abstract: AI is moving from assisting people to automating work: AI agents now call internal systems, run scripts and take actions on their own. This white paper brings together AI automation, AI security and AI governance. It argues that organizations should shift from asking “Is this AI model safe?” to “What can this AI model reach?” Because no one can perfectly guarantee an AI model’s behavior, it recommends containing agentic AI through sandboxing, least-privilege access and a Zero Trust mindset that treats model output as untrusted data. The paper reviews common threats to AI models (espionage, sabotage and fraud) and sets out a governance approach covering accountability, AI inventory, approval gates for high-impact actions, testing before and after change, audit trails and incident response. It explains the relevance to U.S. national interests, including critical infrastructure and its alignment with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and America’s AI Action Plan, and closes with practical best practices. It is intended for quality engineers, software engineers, security practitioners and program managers working with AI-enabled applications.

It argues that organizations should shift from asking “Is this AI model safe?” to “What can this AI model reach?” Because no one can perfectly guarantee an AI model’s behavior, it recommends containing agentic AI through sandboxing, least-privilege access and a Zero Trust mindset that treats model output as untrusted data. The paper reviews common threats to AI models (espionage, sabotage and fraud) and sets out a governance approach covering accountability, AI inventory, approval gates for high-impact actions, testing before and after change, audit trails and incident response. It explains the relevance to U.S. national interests, including critical infrastructure and its alignment with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and America’s AI Action Plan, and closes with practical best practices. It is intended for quality engineers, software engineers, security practitioners and program managers working with AI-enabled applications.

title: A Rewrite That Keeps the Label Has Already Read It: Why an LLM Paraphrase Can Raise a Sentiment Classifier's Accuracy Without the Classifier Getting Better, Four Accounts of the Gain, and the Re-Annotation and Neutral-Rate Controls That Would Separate Them
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. A 2026 study reports that sentiment classifiers score higher on reviews rewritten by small language models than on the human originals, by up to 5.8 accuracy points, and reads the gain as stylistic alignment: the rewrite strips idiosyncrasy and hands the classifier text closer to what it was trained on. It concludes that benchmarks cleaned or paraphrased by language models will overstate classifier performance. Two older literatures point the other way. Paraphrase and style-transfer attacks drive the same classifiers down, and a 2025 study of fifty thousand rephrased tweets finds that rewriting pulls sentiment toward neutral, a pull its robustness checks found again when the prompt asked for the sentiment to be kept. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that neither direction measures the classifier alone, because every one of these designs scores the rewritten text against the label of the text it replaced. The paper separates four accounts of a rewrite-induced gain: alignment of style with the classifier's training data; a fall in the rate of neutral predictions, which the anchor's scoring counts as errors; the paraphraser acting as an annotator that decides the polarity and then writes it plainly; and the removal of hard, mixed and ironic items. It shows from the anchor's released code that its prompt demands one of two polarities and that a neutral prediction is always scored wrong, that its own count of label flips is mislabelled: the printed 291 is the net gain, not the number of improvements, and that a test-time rewriting study found rewritten inputs still sitting with the out-of-distribution data in embedding space. The paper consolidates the measured values in two tables and a figure, states a licensing procedure as an algorithm, counts from the anchor's released predictions that a fall in neutral predictions carries about half of the largest gain, and names the re-annotation, paraphraser-baseline and prompt-ablation controls that would settle which account holds for the rest.

title: Finite Nonlinear Mixing: Exact Bounds (R2.1)
abstract: Original explanatory preprint for the finite SIGMA nonlinear mixing model. It derives conservation, nonnegativity and a complete-step contraction under an explicit uniform positive-mixing assumption; reproduces a constant-fraction rational trajectory and its closed-form decomposition; and distinguishes injective from non-injective contrast maps with exact cases. The results concern a declared finite mathematical model, not measured transport, chemistry, physical validation or a claim of mathematical novelty. Implementation tests are not substituted for proof. This deposit contains only the original PDF; no source code, earlier archive or third-party figures are included. title: Geospatial analysis for optimal solar power plant siting in industrial zones
abstract: This study integrates Geographic Information Systems (GIS) with the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to optimally identify locations for the establishment of solar power plants within Industrial zones across Iran. The principal innovation of this research lies in its evaluation of industrial zones as open land suitable for utility-scale, ground-mounted solar power plant deployment. Unlike most previous studies, which have primarily focused on undeveloped natural land such as barren or agricultural areas or built structures such as rooftops and dam reservoirs, this study emphasizes the strategic value of existing industrial infrastructure in solar power plant siting. For this purpose, eleven key criteria in three domains technical, economic, and environmental were carefully weighted and analyzed using AHP method. After conducting spatial modeling and integrating the layers within the ArcGIS environment, the total solar potential of the country was determined. The results indicated that the provinces of Kerman (5430 TWh/year), Sistan and Baluchestan (4937 TWh/year), Razavi Khorasan (4583 TWh/year), and Fars (4448 TWh/year) possess the highest theoretical capacities for solar energy production. Additionally, the analysis of overlap between industrial zones and high-radiation areas revealed that provinces such as Yazd, Kerman, Isfahan, and Qom demonstrate more than 60% overlap, offering substantial potential for the successful implementation of solar projects. These findings provide a strategic framework for renewable energy policymaking at the national level, as well as valuable insights for private sector decision-making in solar energy investments.

title: From Context to Code : Constraint Memory as Executable Checks in Agent Organizations
abstract: Agent organisations, made of planners, workers, checkers and human approvers, are increasingly assembled by pairing a workflow engine with an agent runtime. This paper studies one such pairing, a LangGraph state graph driving the OpenClaw agent runtime, on a real business task. Against a single-agent baseline on the same platform and model, the organisation spent 23.8 times the tokens and about eleven times the wall-clock time to produce one monthly management report. The cause was structural. The graph opened a new agent session at every step, so 49 sessions each rebuilt the job’s memory by re-reading files that a single agent reads once. We make three contributions. First, we measure the cost of what Ning et al. (2026) call implicit shared state. In the heaviest sessions, reconstructed memory made up 41% of what the agents read but 60% of the tool context they carried, because it was read early and re-sent with every later call. Second, we name the fault that produced it, the one-to-one mapping of workflow steps onto agent sessions, and express its cost in a simple model of agent memory. Third, we propose that one part of agent memory, its constraints, should not live in context at all. In a sample of the job’s instruction text, about three quarters of the rules the agents were asked to remember could be written as executable checks, and one rule was restated 31 times across seven files. We call this constraint memory as code. A foundry step compiles rules into checks, a check library accumulates them across jobs, and the checks run inside the worker and at the points where defects spread. Prior work already stores procedures as code and enforces safety policies as code. What is new here is treating an agent’s accumulated rules as a memory tier whose natural form is a check, chosen for cost and for resilience to compaction. Our data suggest that the direct context saving is modest, about a tenth of carried tool context, while the larger gains lie in replacing model-based verification and preventing rework. We state these claims as testable hypotheses and give a protocol for testing them. Keywords: agent memory, constraint memory, code as harness, multi-agent systems, OpenClaw, LangGraph, context engineering, token economics, runtime verification Author’s note: the problem, ideas and direction of the analysis are the author’s; Claude (Anthropic) assisted with analysis, drafting, figures and formatting. See the declaration on the use of AI before the references.

title: UPI Fraud Intelligence & Analytics Dashboard
authors: Dr. Manoj Singh Sayyed Alaa Mariya Irfan
abstract: The widespread use of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has made digital payments faster and more accessible, while also increasing the need to examine reported fraud in a structured way. Much of the existing UPI fraud literature studies machine-learning or deep-learning techniques that classify or predict fraudulent transactions. This paper describes the UPI Fraud Intelligence Analytics Dashboard, a dataset-driven platform for analysing records that have already been labelled as fraudulent. The dashboard analyses records by state, bank, fraud type, transaction amount, and time. It also supports individual transaction checks, automatic statistical findings, and analysis of compatible uploaded files. The prototype uses Flask and Pandas on the backend and HTML, JavaScript, Bootstrap, and Chart.js on the frontend. Its findings are calculated from the loaded records; it does not generate a fraud probability or claim to identify fraud independently. The paper outlines the platform design, processing workflow, analytical features, and a functional evaluation using the supplied dataset.

title: TASNIFI VA ULARNI DASTURIY TEGLASH TAMOYILLARI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Maqolada Oʻzbek tili milliy korpusida qisqartmalarni avtomatik aniqlash va teglashning nazariy-uslubiy hamda dasturiy tamoyillari chuqur tadqiq etilgan. Korpus lingvistikasi yondashuvlari va dasturiy modullar asosida qisqartmalarni qayta ishlash modelini ishlab chiqib, uning ilmiy-amaliy samaradorligini asoslagan. Kalit soʻzlar: kompyuter lingvistikasi, Oʻzbek tili milliy korpusi, qisqartma, teglash, korpus, leksikografiya, dasturiy ta'minot, lingvistik tahlil. Аннотация. В статье глубоко исследованы теоретико-методологические и программные принципы автоматического распознавания и теггирования сокращений в Национальном корпусе узбекского языка. На основе подходов корпусной лингвистики и программных модулей разработана модель обработки аббревиатур, а также обоснована ее научно-практическая эффективность. Ключевые слова: компьютерная лингвистика, Национальный корпус узбекского языка, аббревиатура, теггирование, корпус, лексикография, программное обеспечение, лингвистический анализ. Abstract. The article deeply investigates the theoretical, methodological, and software principles of automatic identification and tagging of abbreviations in the National Corpus of the Uzbek Language. Based on corpus linguistics approaches and software modules, a model for processing abbreviations was developed, and its scientific and practical effectiveness was substantiated. Keywords: computational linguistics, National Corpus of the Uzbek Language, abbreviation, tagging, corpus, lexicography, software, linguistic analysis

title: AUGMANITAI Data Catalog and Web Integration, version 0.1: DCAT and schema.org Description of the Persistently Identified AUGMANITAI Datasets
abstract: Machine-readable data catalog (W3C DCAT and schema.org DataCatalog/Dataset) of the archived datasets of the AUGMANITAI research programme: the AUGMANITAI core vocabulary, the oversight record vocabulary, the AUGMANITAI dimensions register and the MANITAI field atlas. Each dataset entry gives its persistent identifier under https://w3id.org/augmanitai/, its DOI, version, languages, licence where applicable and download addresses with media types. The package also contains the bilingual (German/English) page "MANITAI in the web", which explains openly how the AUGMANITAI language of terms is woven into the internet: persistent addresses, frozen versions, archive with fingerprints and time stamps, formats for machines, a reading for language models and software agents, and the data catalog. title: Asynchronous Magic State Cultivation: Variable-Metric Lindbladian Dynamics, Topological Code Grafting, and the Quantum Silicon Paradox
abstract: The primary barrier to fault-tolerant universal quantum computing is the Eastin-Knill theorem, which precludes transversal implementation of universal logical gates. Conventional architectures circumvent this restriction via magic state distillation factories that consume upwards of 90%-95% of physical processor spacetime volume. Recently, Google Quantum AI demonstrated Magic State Cultivation on the Willow processor, achieving a 40x error reduction and 99.99% logical T-state fidelity by dynamically growing states in a localized patch and grafting them from a distance-3 color code into a distance-5 surface code. However, physical realization revealed a fundamental temporal conflict: external, rigid affine clock schedules clash with low-frequency cryostat thermal cycles and electrical drift, causing control-plane desynchronization—a quantum manifestation of the Silicon Paradox. In this monograph, we establish a unified theoretical framework resolving this bottleneck. Lifting open quantum evolution to variable-metric temporal manifolds (dτ = λ(t)dt), we derive the Variable-Metric Lindblad Master Equation under the Dubins-Schwarz theorem. We prove that state purification speeds and Bures transport bounds scale directly with physical non-equilibrium entropy dissipation. We formalize color-to-surface code grafting as an isometric manifold transition, establishing that boundary gauge constraints prevent parametric fault divergence. Finally, adapting the Byzantine Kenosis Protocol from distributed consensus architectures, we demonstrate that intermediate syndrome checks allow non-correctable fault trajectories to be quarantined at the threshold in O(1) operations, eliminating recursive distillation trees.

title: Classifying Automated Driving Systems Using Telematics Data: A Comparative Study of GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Models
abstract: The rapid advancement of sensing, artificial intelligence, and in-vehicle computing has accelerated deployment of automated driving systems (ADSs). As vehicles move toward software-defined architectures, multiple driving stacks—including manufacturer and aftermarket solutions—may coexist, raising the need to verify which system is actively controlling the vehicle from observable behavior alone. This paper investigates ADS identification using only harmonized vehicle telematics, without proprietary controller states or perception sensors. We compared three deep sequence models—Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and a Transformer Encoder—for distinguishing Comma Openpilot, Tesla Autopilot, Cadillac Super Cruise, and manual driving from eleven shared features over 32-timestep windows. On clean held-out data, all three architectures achieved strong performance (macro-F1 above 0.91; mean ± std over 20 random seeds), with the Transformer Encoder attaining the highest mean macro-F1 and the GRU providing competitive, lower-cost alternatives. We further evaluated robustness under a structured telematics noise framework covering six atomic threat families and four compound multi-fault conditions at different severity levels using a two-arm protocol over 7 random seeds: clean training (Arm A) versus evaluation matched noise-augmented training (Arm B). Under clean training, degradation was highly threat-dependent: correlated cross-feature noise and stochastic drift—and their compounds—caused the largest absolute and relative drops in macro-F1, whereas delay-with-hold temporal jitter and temporal delay had comparatively minor effects. This pattern is shared across GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Encoder models. Evaluation matched augmentation preserved clean-test accuracy while substantially reducing degradation, including at held-out severities and on compound faults withheld from training. The results show that telemetry-based ADS identification is feasible at scale and that reliable deployment requires explicit attention to continuous and cross-feature impairments.

evidence.title: Classifying Automated Driving Systems Using Telematics Data: A Comparative Study of GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Models
evidence.abstract: The rapid advancement of sensing, artificial intelligence, and in-vehicle computing has accelerated deployment of automated driving systems (ADSs). As vehicles move toward software-defined architectures, multiple driving stacks—including manufacturer and aftermarket solutions—may coexist, raising the need to verify which system is actively controlling the vehicle from observable behavior alone. This paper investigates ADS identification using only harmonized vehicle telematics, without proprietary controller states or perception sensors. We compared three deep sequence models—Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and a Transformer Encoder—for distinguishing Comma Openpilot, Tesla Autopilot, Cadillac Super Cruise, and manual driving from eleven shared features over 32-timestep windows. On clean held-out data, all three architectures achieved strong performance (macro-F1 above 0.91; mean ± std over 20 random seeds), with the Transformer Encoder attaining the highest mean macro-F1 and the GRU providing competitive, lower-cost alternatives. We further evaluated robustness under a structured telematics noise framework covering six atomic threat families and four compound multi-fault conditions at different severity levels using a two-arm protocol over 7 random seeds: clean training (Arm A) versus evaluation matched noise-augmented training (Arm B). Under clean training, degradation was highly threat-dependent: correlated cross-feature noise and stochastic drift—and their compounds—caused the largest absolute and relative drops in macro-F1, whereas delay-with-hold temporal jitter and temporal delay had comparatively minor effects. This pattern is shared across GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Encoder models. Evaluation matched augmentation preserved clean-test accuracy while substantially reducing degradation, including at held-out severities and on compound faults withheld from training. The results show that telemetry-based ADS identification is feasible at scale and that reliable deployment requires explicit attention to continuous and cross-feature impairments.

title: A2A-RefGuard: A Novel Reference-closure Noninterference Algorithm for Detecting Cross-principal State Leakage in Agent2Agent Systems
abstract: Agent2Agent systems maintain state across tasks, contexts, references, continuation, history, artifacts, and streaming operations.This creates a security problem in which protected state owned by one principal may indirectly influence an observation available to another principal even when direct access is denied.This paper introduces A2A RefGuard, a novel verification algorithm based on Reference Closure Noninterference.The method combines paired state intervention, protocol derived reference closure, source specific authorization, and observer output comparison to identify unauthorized cross principal state influence.Evaluation included a controlled benchmark, an independently constructed execution oracle, mixed authority cases, evidence quality stress tests, protocol backed replay, ablation analysis, and scalability testing.A2A RefGuard achieved perfect classification in the controlled and independent evaluations, eliminated false positives produced by source insensitive alternatives, and processed graphs containing up to ten thousand tasks with low runtime and memory overhead.

title: Differential Privacy Tradeoffs in Large-Scale ML Model Training
abstract: Differential privacy (DP) provides the gold standard for formal privacy guarantees in machine learning, offering mathematically rigorous bounds on the information an adversary can infer about any individual training record from an observed model.However, the practical application of differential privacy to large-scale ML model training -including billion-parameter language models, large vision models, and complex multimodal systems -involves a complex web of trade-offs between privacy budget expenditure, model utility, computational efficiency, and regulatory compliance that remains poorly understood at production scale.This paper presents a comprehensive empirical and theoretical analysis of differential privacy trade-offs in large-scale ML training, examining how privacy budget (epsilon), model scale, dataset size, batch size, and training duration interact to determine the achievable privacy-utility Pareto frontier.We introduce DPOptimizer, a privacy budget allocation framework that maximizes model utility for a given privacy budget through adaptive noise calibration, layer-wise privacy amplification, and optimal composition strategies.DPOptimizer achieves utility improvements of 23-41% over standard DP-SGD configurations across GPT-2, BERT, ResNet-152, and ViT-L models, while maintaining identical formal privacy guarantees.We further provide the first systematic analysis of how the privacy-utility-compute trilemma scales with model size from 10M to 70B parameters, offering practical deployment guidelines for organizations navigating regulatory requirements under GDPR, HIPAA, and emerging AIspecific privacy legislation.

title: A BERT-based multi-task learning framework for social media opinion mining with risk detection
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a BERT-based multi-task learning framework for social media mining and risk detection. Unlike traditional open-loop architectures, the proposed system establishes a closed-loop feedback mechanism among crawling, analysis, and alerting modules, focusing on high-accuracy negative sentiment detection for social risk detection. A dataset of 4,238 texts is constructed, covering eight topic categories and three sentiment labels. A BERT-based multi-task framework with shared encoder and two task-specific heads jointly optimizes topic classification and sentiment analysis. Training uses AdamW (learning rate 2e-5, batch size 16, max length 128) for three epochs. The multi-task BERT model achieves 97.97% F1 for topic classification and 99.89% F1 for sentiment analysis. Negative sentiment detection reaches 100% accuracy. Compared to single-task models (98.34% and 99.76%), the multi-task model maintains comparable topic performance while improving sentiment analysis. Removing pre-training fine-tuning reduces training time by 7.9% with stable performance. The model performs two tasks in one inference, reducing deployment complexity while enabling reliable negative sentiment detection for social media opinion monitoring.

title: Dimensional Input Parameter Language (DIPL): Language Specification, Version 1.0.0
abstract: DIPL (Dimensional Input Parameter Language) is a declarative language for describing structured input parameters for scientific and numerical software. It brings parameter values, data types, physical units, constraints, metadata, and relationships into one human-readable format. This specification defines DIPL’s syntax, type system, expression and unit semantics, schemas, validation, and execution model. It is intended for language users and implementers and serves as the reference for the SNT implementation. It includes a formal grammar and examples of the language’s main constructs.

title: AI-Driven Personalization in Digital Marketing: Consumer Trust, Engagement, and Purchase Behavior - A Systematic Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization has increasingly transformed digital marketing by enabling firms to deliver individualized recommendations, content, and offers based on consumer data and behavioral patterns. However, the growing use of personalization also raises important questions regarding consumer trust, engagement, and purchase behavior. This study aims to conduct a systematic literature review (SLR) of research on AI-driven personalization in digital marketing to examine its implications for consumer trust, engagement, and purchase behavior. Using Scopus as the primary database, the search process identified 2,906 records and, through successive filtering and screening procedures, resulted in 51 eligible studies. Bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and thematic synthesis were employed to identify publication trends, intellectual structures, and key research themes. The findings indicate a shift from technology-oriented research toward consumer-centered perspectives, with increasing attention to consumer experience, trust, engagement, privacy, transparency, purchase intention, and purchase behavior. The review further demonstrates that the effectiveness of AI-driven personalization is context-dependent and influenced by consumer perceptions and data-related concerns. These findings provide an integrated basis for understanding the evolving role of AI personalization in contemporary digital marketing

title: A Demand-Side Benchmark for Consumer-Facing Construction Cost Questions: Price-Figure Span, Output Consistency, and the Case for a Verifiable Reference Layer
abstract: Consumers facing home-renovation quotes operate in a credence-goods market: they cannot verify whether a quoted price is fair, and general-purpose large language models (LLMs) are now a zero-cost place to ask. Whether LLM answers are actionable for this purpose is untested. Demand-side benchmarks exist for medical, legal, and financial advice, but not for construction costs. We present, to our knowledge, the first consumer-question benchmark for construction costs: a fixed public question set with public scoring rules that characterizes answer properties, not a comparison against ground-truth prices. Forty Japanese renovation-price questions were posed to frontier LLMs, with repeated-trial sets measuring output stability. A matched re-run at bare provider defaults with a current frontier model (GPT-5.5) removes a settings confound in the original configuration. We separate two quantities. The headline range that a model states as the going rate has a median width of 2.5× to 3×. The full set of price figures in the same answer, including itemized components and unit rates, spans a median of 10× at bare defaults; this is the dispersion a reader must integrate. No LLM answer volunteered an over-charge decision threshold, although no question asked for one. Across five repeated runs, the headline range of GPT-5.5 stayed within 1.5× on 15 of 20 everyday questions, while on the widest questions, its endpoints moved by up to 5×. A deterministic structured engine over an open cost database is included as existence proof that a citable reference layer is constructible; its accuracy is not validated here. All questions, raw outputs, harnesses, and scoring codes are public.

title: Decomposing Apparent Skill in Machine-Learning Event Classification: A Multi-Catalog Study of Label Structure, Feature Coupling, and Operational Generalization
abstract: Machine-learning evaluation assumes that a held-out target represents the decision problem of interest. That assumption is difficult to satisfy when labels are constructed retrospectively from the same observational record that supplies the predictors, because a classifier can then reproduce regularities embedded in the target-generation procedure rather than resolve the harder decision. We treat earthquake event-role classification as an experimental case study of this problem and develop a diagnostic decomposition of apparent skill. Three catalogs differing in size, completeness, and feature availability are evaluated with chronologically partitioned gradient-boosted classifiers under a common window-defined target, and conventional held-out performance is decomposed using structural magnitude baselines, feature-family ablation, evaluation conditioned on the information state, synthetic epidemic-type-aftershock-sequence procedural nulls, alternative target definitions, probability calibration, conformal prediction, and cross-catalog transfer. Pooled discrimination was high, at ROC AUC 0.889 to 0.972, but fell by 0.264 to 0.387 when evaluation was restricted to events whose role is unresolved by preceding local magnitude ordering. A single magnitude-difference statistic came within 0.006 of the fitted models in two catalogs and exceeded them in the third, and removing the magnitude feature family reduced discrimination by 0.10 to 0.16. Synthetic catalogs generated without parent–offspring magnitude dependence reproduced both the high pooled score and its contraction under conditioning. Calibration, conformal coverage, and transfer behaviour changed independently of discrimination. The contribution is a reproducible diagnostic framework for interpreting machine-learning performance on retrospectively constructed scientific targets.

title: A Comparative Study of Client-Level Stabilization Techniques in Federated Learning for Robust Plant Disease Recognition
abstract: The successful integration of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in precision agriculture provided farmers with the means to identify potential issues, such as early disease detection or pest infestations, by making crop-related predictions. The new technological developments in this field improve the functioning of traditional agriculture by reducing the dependence on specialized human expertise and facilitating greater access to diagnostic procedures. However, most studies conducted in this area rely on centralized training of AI models, which leads to increased costs and raised privacy-related concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a compelling framework for collaboratively training machine learning (ML) models on distributed datasets without centralizing the data owned by each participant. FL offers significant advantages in the preservation of data privacy, facilitates the collaborative exploitation of geographically distributed data sources, and reduces the risks associated with centralized collection. In this paper, we investigate the current limitations and performance boundaries of existing Federated and privacy-preserving learning in distributed sensing systems for plant disease detection, in scenarios that closely resemble real-world conditions. Our analysis specifically examined how FL aggregation algorithms, such as FedAvg, FedAvgM and FedProx, work in a custom multi-client experimental setup where data is partitioned so that each participant observes only those symptom patterns associated with specific environmental and climatic conditions. We propose further partial aggregation of the local model, an approach where we send only the model backbone to the central server, while the classification head of each participant remains strictly on the client side. The construction of environmentally heterogeneity is combined with a globally representative stabilizer node designed to preserve knowledge across disease classes that may be absent from certain clients.

title: Intelligent Retrieval of Corresponding Engineering Standard Clauses for Cross-Border Construction Projects
abstract: Cross-border construction projects increasingly involve heterogeneous engineering standards from different national systems, creating challenges for standards comparison and compliance assessment. Existing approaches largely rely on textual similarity or syntactic matching, which may be insufficient for identifying semantically corresponding technical provisions. This study proposes an engineering-aware intelligent retrieval framework for identifying potentially corresponding clauses across national engineering standards. The framework integrates multilingual semantic embeddings with engineering-specific terminology, numerical information, and topic-based search-space constraints to retrieve and rank candidate clauses for subsequent expert comparison. The methodology was evaluated using a controlled benchmark comprising 105 manually aligned Chinese–Uzbek engineering clause pairs across 11 engineering topics. The results achieved a Top-1 Accuracy of 62.9% and a Recall@5 of 91.4%, demonstrating the feasibility of automated retrieval for identifying semantically corresponding engineering provisions. The findings suggest that engineering-specific information can provide constraints beyond general semantic similarity and substantially narrow the candidate search space in cross-standard clause retrieval. The proposed framework is intended as a decision-support layer preceding expert interpretation rather than as a substitute for technical judgment or regulatory compliance assessment. It provides an initial methodological basis for improving the efficiency and consistency of cross-standard comparison and for supporting the digital management of heterogeneous engineering standards in cross-border construction projects.

title: A Web Engineering Approach to AI-Enabled Japanese Tutoring via Instructional Design Pattern Mining
abstract: Despite the proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled web applications for Japanese language learning, existing platforms suffer from three critical challenges: insufficient integration of AI capabilities with pedagogical design, limited scenario adaptability across proficiency levels, and suboptimal lightweight deployment on the browser side. To address these gaps and explore instructional design patterns tailored to diverse Japanese learning needs, this study focuses on web application technology implementation and interaction design as the core analytical dimensions. Three typical AI-enabled Japanese tutoring web applications were selected as research objects, and 192 Japanese learners participated in the empirical research. Quantitative data were obtained through technical disassembly, questionnaire surveys, and web-based behavior tracking; learning effects were verified by comparative experiments, and the weight of instructional design elements was determined via the analytic hierarchy process, finally extracting core instructional design modes suitable for the mainstream Japanese learning stages from beginner to upper-intermediate (Japanese-Language Proficiency Test [JLPT] N5–N2), with preliminary applicability discussion for the advanced stage (N1 and above). The results show that web-based lightweight AI technology deployment and real-time AI interactive feedback design are the core elements, with a combined weight of over 40%. There is a significant positive correlation between web-based AI technology implementation and user satisfaction, with the highest implementation effect and user acceptance in listening, speaking, and grammar modules. title: A TRACEABLE DETERMINISTIC DECISION SYSTEM FOR CURRICULUM-BASED ELIGIBILITY ASSESSMENT
abstract: This study develops and evaluates a traceable deterministic decision system for curriculum-based eligibility assessment in a virtual-university information system. The problem addressed is the need to transform documented curricular requirements into an executable decision rule while keeping rule construction separate from subsequent evaluation against reference labels. The system represents semester-status conditions and an ECTS threshold as an explicit deterministic predicate, validates and locks the specification before execution, and records the resulting decision for each case. Evaluation was conducted on a controlled corpus of 100 cases. The system produced 20 ELIGIBLE and 80 NOT_ELIGIBLE decisions, with TN=80, FP=0, FN=0, and TP=20. Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, Specificity, Balanced Accuracy, and MCC were all 1.000000, with a 95% confidence interval of [0.963007, 1.000000] for Accuracy. The results establish agreement for the evaluated corpus and protocol, not generalization to other curricula or cohorts.

title: Group Shapley values, with application to bond recovery rate prediction
abstract: Grouped feature attribution is increasingly important in high-dimensional applications, where predictors often belong to economically or scientifically meaningful categories and individual SHAP values can become too granular for reliable interpretation. This paper develops a formal inferential framework for assessing whether group-level SHAP-style attributions are statistically significant and complements it with a tree-based grouped implementation for ensemble models. The proposed testing procedure is based on a three-cumulant chi-square approximation and is designed for challenging settings involving high dimensionality, skewness, sparsity, feature dependence, and limited sample size. Simulation results show that the proposed test maintains accurate empirical size and often achieves higher power than competing alternatives such as the Wald and CQ tests. The framework is applied to bond recovery rate prediction using a global dataset from 1996 to 2023 with 2094 observations and 98 features organized into 16 subgroups and five broader categories: bond characteristics, firm fundamentals, industry-specific factors, market-related variables, and macroeconomic indicators. The empirical results identify market-related variables and bond characteristics as the most influential groups. Overall, the paper contributes a statistically rigorous approach to global inference on grouped SHAP-style importance measures and illustrates its practical value in a financial prediction setting.

title: Adaptive federated ensemble learning with hyperparameter optimization for distributed healthcare IoT
abstract: The rapid evolution of IoT-enabled healthcare systems has resulted in large-scale distributed data generation across various institutions. While federated learning enables collaborative model training without centralized data, it degrades non-identical data distributions and statistical imbalance across clients. Moreover, the convergence instability and hyperparameter sensitivity remain critical challenges in heterogeneous healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Stability-Aware Secure Federated Ensemble Framework integrated with LampyraCetacea Optimization (ASEFE-LCO). The platform integrates FedAvg and FedProx algorithms with an adaptive multi-model ensemble mechanism to ensure convergence stability under non-IID conditions. To enhance predictive robustness, LampyraCetacea Optimization is employed for dynamic hyperparameter adaptation in non-convex environments. To offer formal privacy tamper-proof protection, an integrated blockchain layer is applied to ensure decentralized auditability. The proposed architecture offers an end-to-end intelligent platform that combines optimization stability, security assurance, scalability, and distributed knowledge integration. As a core tenet of the proposed model, the experimental evaluation of the IoT healthcare security benchmark dataset achieves 99.94% accuracy, indicating a robust, secure, and clinically interpretable solution for an intelligent healthcare system.

title: An IoT-based approach for solar irradiance estimation using three different sensor proxies
abstract: High-precision Commercial pyranometers and radiometers are often prohibitively expensive, and inexpensive solar power meters lack integrated wireless connectivity, limiting deployment in decentralized monitoring networks. This feasibility study presents a budget-friendly IoT-based sensing platform designed to estimate global horizontal solar irradiance (W/m 2 ) using a multi-model fusion technique. The hardware architecture utilizes a NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller to continuously acquire real-time data from three distinct, non-intrusive radiometric proxies: (i) differential surface temperature measured using black (T2) and white (T3) aluminum plates. (ii) optical illuminance (lux) via a BH1750 digital ambient light photo-diode and (iii) electrical short-circuit current drift via a polycrystalline photovoltaic (PV) panel monitored by an INA219 sensor. To eliminate manual logging errors and ensure synchronization, sensor streams are telemetered in real time to a centralized workstation using TCP/IP socket connections. The proxies were calibrated and empirically cross-validated against a commercial reference radiometer (HTC LX-107) under dynamic outdoor solar radiation conditions. Regression models demonstrated strong statistical alignment between proxy signals and absolute solar irradiance. Outdoor validation confirmed that the optical illuminance proxy achieved the highest dynamic responsiveness (R² = 0.69 to 0.94 and RMSE ≈ 51.32 to 115.03 W/m²), followed closely by the differential temperature proxy (R² = 0.81 to 0.88 and RMSE ≈ 70.82 to 94.92 W/m²). The PV panel electrical proxy also demonstrated a strong predictive performance and maintained a solid peak multi-regression fit during outdoor validation (R² = 0.68 to 0.77 and RMSE ≈ 103.06 to 117.45 W/m²). The proposed multi-modal IoT framework offers an automated, scalable, and budget-friendly alternative to standard pyranometers. By combining multi-sensor fusion with automated wireless telemetry, the system successfully tracks diurnal irradiance fluctuations, providing a viable tool for solar energy management, agricultural microclimate monitoring, and smart grid integration at a fraction of the cost of commercial hardware.

title: Physical Space Modelling for Reconfigurable Interacting Systems
abstract: Abstract Multi-agent systems operating in shared physical environments require coordination, reconfiguration, and navigation mechanisms that depend on spatial locality and dynamic interaction contexts. Existing process calculi for distributed systems often abstract away from physical space, making it difficult to model systems in which communication and mobility are constrained by the environment. This paper introduces sparc , a spatial process calculus for modelling reconfigurable multi-agent systems in structured environments. The calculus integrates spatial structure, attribute-based communication, and mobility within a unified framework, enabling agents to communicate locally, adapt their behaviour according to environmental information, and navigate structured spaces without requiring global knowledge of the environment.

title: A drift-limited length law for authorship attribution: code, pre-registration documents and results
abstract: Code, pre-registration documents, SHA-256 fingerprints and results for the manuscript “How much reference text is worth collecting? A drift-limited length law for authorship attribution” (I. Avcibas, OSTIM Technical University, submitted to JASIST, 2026). Two pre-registered experiments on Project Gutenberg novels (English, French, German; then new English and French authors and Italian) with a cross-work design and a full grid of questioned length, reference length per candidate and number of candidates (168 cells per language, classifier and word-list size, 200 repetitions per author). The archive holds the corpus builders with the fixed selection rule and the list of every work used (Gutenberg numbers), the run and analysis scripts, the pre-registrations written before the runs with their SHA-256 locks, the raw counts, the fitted models and verdicts, and the LaTeX source of the manuscript with the scripts that generate every number and table. The texts themselves are not included; the scripts download them from Project Gutenberg.

title: Operations of Mind: A framework for emergent thinking
abstract: Thinking is not hardcoded, and it cannot be. This note sets out Operations of Mind (OoM), a framework inwhich a machine is not given a method of thinking but a small set of basic mental operations, a drive tomake sense of what it encounters, and the freedom to chain those operations itself. OoM divides thoughtinto two deliberate layers: an inner layer that runs continuously and cheaply, and an active layer thatreasons deliberately on harder problems. It sits on two earlier pieces of the LOCUS programme, theCoherent World Hypothesis (CWH), which serves as its imagination, and the Repertoire Hypothesis, whichserves as its memory. The central bet is that thinking does not have to be trained into a machine; it canemerge from a small set of basic mental operations, chained under a drive to make sense. First tests ingenerated worlds give early support: operation chains grown from use beat chains built blindly, the driveignores noise without being told to, and see-then-invent beat a plain counting baseline for the first time,with a control showing the gain tracks real hidden structure. The gains are small, about 1.5 points ofroughly 5 learnable in a 60-step budget, and the active layer is untested. This note is a framework withpreliminary evidence, not a validated result.

title: Victims and Producers?
abstract: The prevention of hate speech is one of the main challenges faced by today's complex and multicultural societies. This exploratory study, based on a quantitative methodology, provides a diagnosis of the incidence of hate speech in a sample of Primary Education degree students at a Spanish university. The results indicate that 94.4% of participants reported having witnessed hate speech, compared to 46.1% who stated they had suffered it and 25% who admitted to having emitted hateful comments. Furthermore, our hypothesis is supported, as a significant -though not majority- percentage of participants both produce and suffer hate speech, given that hate is a problem linked to structural inequalities present in society and to social polarization fueled by the Internet and social media. The findings also confirm the need to work with preservice primary teachers to prevent hate speech in classrooms.

title: Benchmarking Arabic Transformer‐Based Language Model Embeddings for Document Clustering: A Comparative Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advances in transformer‐based language models have substantially improved semantic text representations for Arabic natural language processing. However, their effectiveness for unsupervised document clustering has not been comprehensively investigated across different clustering algorithms, preprocessing strategies and document representations. This study presents a comparative evaluation of six transformer‐based embedding models, namely AraGPT2, arabertv0.2, CAMeLBERT, AraELECTRA, AraBERTv2, and Multilingual‐MiniLM, together with a TF‐IDF lexical baseline, for Arabic document clustering. The evaluation was conducted on five Arabic datasets spanning both general‐domain and domain‐specific corpora using four clustering algorithms: K ‐Means++, Spherical K ‐Means, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HAC) and Spectral Co‐Clustering. To investigate the influence of text representation, six preprocessing configurations were considered by varying stemming and document‐length reduction strategies. Clustering performance was assessed using Normalised Mutual Information (NMI), Accuracy, Purity, Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Macro F 1‐score, V‐Measure and Entropy. Furthermore, the experimental results were statistically validated using the Friedman test, average‐rank analysis, and Holm‐corrected Wilcoxon signed‐rank post hoc comparisons. The experimental results demonstrate that preserving the original lexical and morphological structure of Arabic text generally yields superior clustering performance for contextual embedding models compared with light stemming. The influence of document length was found to be dataset‐ and representation‐dependent, with full‐document representations achieving the strongest overall performance, while shorter representations frequently remained competitive. TF‐IDF provided a strong lexical baseline, particularly for general‐domain datasets. Among the evaluated embedding models, AraBERTv2 achieved the best overall average rank, closely followed by arabertv0.2, and the post hoc statistical analysis revealed no significant difference between the two models. CAMeLBERT consistently exhibited stable and competitive performance across all datasets, whereas AraELECTRA produced the weakest clustering results. From the clustering perspective, Spherical K ‐Means demonstrated the most consistent overall performance, while HAC achieved the highest clustering quality in several of the best‐performing embedding configurations. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive benchmark for transformer‐based Arabic document clustering and offers practical guidance for selecting embedding models, preprocessing strategies, document representations, and clustering algorithms for unsupervised Arabic text analysis.
